findings.title: The one cross-thread mutation that actually happens in production — the renderCallbacks closure slots — is still outside the lock
findings.trace: `setCallbacksActive` takes `stateLock` only to swap the boolean (164-167), releases it at 167, then assigns `arView.renderCallbacks.prepareWithDevice` / `.postProcess` at 170-175 (install) or 177-178 (nil) with no synchronization at all. RealityKit reads and invokes those slots on its own render thread every frame. ARP-11's claim named exactly this ('`arView.renderCallbacks` is mutated from the main thread while the render thread may be executing the callbacks it holds', COUNSEL-RAW-OUTPUT-2026-08-11.md:360) and its Proposed direction was install-once + a gated encode; the build rejected that on ADR-035 grounds and substituted a lock that does not reach the closure storage. Reachability is worse than it looks: `uninstall()`/`detach()` is DEAD CODE — `GeoARSessionManager.detach()` (370-387) has no caller anywhere in the app (ARSessionHolder only calls attach/resumeSession/suspendSession at ARSessionHolder.swift:100/104/123). So the field-race the lock closed is unreachable, while the unlocked assignment is the live path: `disarmSemanticMatte()` -> `setCallbacksActive(false)` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:397) on every `suspendSession()` (411), plus the governor's attach/detach at 1141/1144. At suspend the assignment lands BEFORE `arView?.session.pause()` (412), so the render thread is provably still running when the slot is nil'd. Secondary regression: Wave D moved the flag commit ahead of the `guard ... let arView` (166 vs 168), so the flag can now claim `true` while nothing was installed — pre-Wave-D the guard preceded the write.
findings.harm: A Swift closure value is two words (function pointer + context). The main thread stores a new/nil pair into `renderCallbacks.postProcess` while RealityKit's render thread loads and calls it. A torn load (new fn ptr, stale context) or an ARC race (main releases the old closure box between the render thread's load and its call) is EXC_BAD_ACCESS inside the render thread, with a crash log that points into RealityKit and names nothing in this app. Trigger: user walks so a person leaves frame -> 10 s person hysteresis -> 5 s pass-idle -> detach; or leaves the camera tab -> 5 s grace -> suspendSession -> disarmSemanticMatte. Every one of those is a slot store racing a 60 Hz slot read. Per-transition probability is low; across a field population it is a steady trickle against the 99.5% crash-free bar, and it is the exact 'intermittent, timing-dependent, undebuggable from a crash log' class the wave charter targets.
findings.fix: Three steps, cheapest first. (1) Immediately cut exposure: add a minimum-attached dwell and raise the idle-detach delay (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1143 currently 5 s) so a person walking in and out cannot toggle the slots at seconds scale — zero heat cost, ~10x fewer race windows. (2) Pin the actual behavior: run the RENDER-1 stress harness below on device under Thread Sanitizer with SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete. (3) If it reports, adopt ARP-11's original direction — install the callbacks once and early-out inside `encode` on the locked flag — and re-measure ADR-035's cost first: that measurement predates both the current shader early-out (SemanticMatte.metal:147-172) and the current bare-blit idle path (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:427-431), so the 'attached pass with no work' number it rests on is stale. If install-once still loses on heat, do the toggle inside a session pause so the render thread is quiesced.

findings.title: Matte history textures are allocated .private and never initialized; the shader's EMA seeds from undefined GPU memory and a NaN/Inf seed is absorbing
findings.trace: `ensureMatteTextures` creates both matte textures with `storageMode = .private` (445) via `device.makeTexture` (446-449) and writes nothing into them; `matteIndex = 0` (450). On the very next lines `previousMatte = matteTextures[matteIndex]` (304) is bound at texture index 7 (366). The shader reads it unconditionally as the EMA history: `float previous = previousMatte.read(gid).r;` (SemanticMatte.metal:235) then `mix(previous, matte, alpha)` (237) and writes the result back (238). Metal specifies the contents of a newly created texture as undefined; Metal recycles freed allocations inside the process without zeroing, so this is not merely a first-launch concern. Reallocation is routine, not rare: the ARView is constructed at `frame: .zero` (ARSessionHolder.swift:48 and 97) and sized later by SwiftUI, and Wave D's SWE-7 change now animates the camera destination in via `fullScreenCover(item:)` (RootView.swift:60), producing several distinct `context.targetColorTexture` sizes in quick succession — each one re-entering 441-449 and picking up memory just freed by the previous pair.
findings.harm: r16Float has a dense NaN space (exponent 0x1F, non-zero mantissa) and a dense large-finite space. If a seeded pixel is NaN, `mix(NaN, matte, alpha)` is NaN forever — the EMA never converges because NaN is absorbing — and `if (smoothed > 0.01)` (SemanticMatte.metal:240) is false for NaN, so that pixel's occlusion is silently and permanently dead for the whole session: content draws straight over the person/tree there, violating the BRIEF's zero-draw-over-known-front-surface bar with no crash, no log, and no recovery path. If the seed is a large finite value instead, `half(smoothed)` at 249 saturates to inf and `mix` paints a garbage pixel that likewise never decays. Worse, Metal compiles .metal sources with fast-math enabled by default, under which NaN/Inf inputs are undefined rather than merely absorbing. The failure is per-pixel and speckled, so it reads as 'occlusion is flaky on this device' rather than as a bug with a cause.
findings.fix: Do not rely on `isfinite` in the shader — fast-math may fold it away. Add a `historyValid` float to MatteUniforms (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:88-125 / SemanticMatte.metal:14-44), set it to 0 for the first encode after `ensureMatteTextures` allocates and 1 thereafter, and in the kernel use `float previous = (uniforms.historyValid > 0.5) ? previousMatte.read(gid).r : matte;` — three lines, fast-math-proof, and it also removes the visible 3-frame EMA ramp after every resize. Belt: explicitly zero both textures at allocation (a one-shot render pass with loadAction .clear, or `replace(region:)` from a zeroed staging buffer) so the history is defined even if the uniform path is later refactored.

findings.title: The ARP-12 flush only runs while the pass is attached — detaching stops it, and detached is the pass's designed steady state
findings.trace: The per-frame `CVMetalTextureCacheFlush(textureCache, 0)` lives entirely inside `encode` (391, plus the two bail paths at 290 and 300). `setCallbacksActive(false)` (163-180) nils the render callbacks and does nothing else: it does not flush the cache and does not clear `inFlightTextures` (72). `uninstall()` (182-191) nils `pipeline` and empties `matteTextures` but likewise never flushes and never nils `textureCache` (68). So from the instant the governor detaches (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1144, after the 5 s idle at 1143) or `disarmSemanticMatte` fires on suspend (397/411), no flush ever happens again until the pass is re-attached. ADR-035 is the reason detach exists at all, which means the app is designed to spend most of its camera time in precisely the state where the ARP-12 fix is inert. Note the camera session is NOT paused on a governor detach — only on suspend (412) — so ARKit keeps cycling its capture pool the whole time.
findings.harm: A CVMetalTextureCache retains the IOSurface backing of every buffer it has wrapped until Flush recycles the entry; that retention is the documented mechanism ARP-12 identified. At detach time the cache holds entries for the ARKit capture surfaces it wrapped over the preceding frames (capturedImage Y + CbCr, plus segmentation and sceneDepth when person occlusion was on — up to ~4 distinct surfaces). Those stay pinned for the entire detached interval, which can be minutes of walking with no far content. ARKit's capture pool is small; sustained pressure on it drops camera frames in a sawtooth that reads as thermal throttling but isn't — the exact symptom ARP-12 named — and it makes the FT-28/FT-31 heat instrumentation ambiguous for the state the app is in most of the time.
findings.fix: Add a locked `releaseCaptureResources()` that does `inFlightTextures.removeAll(); if let textureCache { CVMetalTextureCacheFlush(textureCache, 0) }`, and call it from the `else` branch of `setCallbacksActive` (177-178) and from `uninstall` (187-190), both under `stateLock`. Take a `flush:` injection seam while you are in there so the behavior is testable without ARKit (Wave C rule 6).

findings.title: prepare(device:) holds stateLock across Metal library load and compute-pipeline creation, so the main actor can block on a shader compile
findings.trace: `prepare(device:)` takes `stateLock` on entry (194-195) and holds it for its whole body, which includes `device.makeDefaultLibrary(bundle: .main)`, `library.makeFunction(name:)` and `device.makeComputePipelineState(function:)` (200-203) plus `CVMetalTextureCacheCreate` (205) and three `makeDummy` calls (206-208). This runs on RealityKit's render thread (installed at 170-172). The main actor takes the same lock at 2.5 Hz from the governor: `setCallbacksActive` locks unconditionally at 164 every tick (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1141 and 1144 are called each tick; the `changed` short-circuit at 168 is AFTER the lock). The class doc asserts 'The lock is held for the whole CPU-side encode (sub-ms); main-actor callers block at worst that long' (53-54) — that claim is false for this path. `ensureMatteTextures` (433-451) is a second, smaller instance of the same shape: it allocates two full-screen r16Float textures (~12 MB total at 1179x2556) under the same lock on every viewport change. Related: the 'Never nest' instruction at line 64 is already violated by `encode`, which holds `stateLock` while entering `SemanticFeed.lock` (242) and `MidFieldDepthFeed.lock` (267) — there is no inversion today because neither feed calls back into the pass, but the comment tells the next author the opposite of what the code does.
findings.harm: `makeComputePipelineState` is a synchronous pipeline compile. Warm (shader cache populated) it is ~1-5 ms; cold — first launch after install or after an OS update, which is every review-flow first run — it is commonly tens to low hundreds of ms. A governor tick landing in that window blocks the MAIN THREAD for that duration: dropped frames and a visible hitch at the exact moment AR occlusion first engages, on a 30 fps target (AppConfig.swift:86) that already has zero headroom against the BRIEF's >=30 fps bar. The comment's 'sub-ms' claim means the next engineer will add work under this lock believing it is free.
findings.fix: Publish, don't build, under the lock: read `device` under the lock, release it, construct library/function/pipeline/cache/dummies into locals, then re-take the lock and commit them only if `pipeline == nil || self.device !== device` still holds (a second builder losing the race just discards its locals). Same shape for `ensureMatteTextures`. Then correct the doc comment at 53-54 and rewrite the 'Never nest' comment at 64 to state the actual invariant: stateLock may be held while acquiring a feed lock, never the reverse.

findings.title: The ARP-12 cure is a full-resolution unpooled IOSurface allocation plus memcpy on the MAIN THREAD at 5 Hz, for pixels Vision immediately throws away
findings.trace: `MidFieldDepthEstimator.update(frame:hz:)` is called from `GeoARSessionManager.frameUpdate()` (2282), which runs on the main actor (class is `@MainActor`, GeoARSessionManager.swift:25-26; the SceneEvents.Update subscription asserts main isolation at 323-327). Both `copyPixelBuffer` calls at 151-152 execute SYNCHRONOUSLY on the main thread, before the `queue.async` hop at 158. Each call does a fresh `CVPixelBufferCreate` with IOSurface backing (208-213) — no CVPixelBufferPool anywhere in the file — followed by a full memcpy of every plane (221-250). With `targetFrameRate = 30` (AppConfig.swift:86) the ARP-6 policy's surviving candidate on A17-class hardware is 1920x1440@30 (GeoARSessionManager.swift:691-696), so `frame.capturedImage` is 1920x1440 4:2:0 biplanar = ~4.15 MB per copy; the LiDAR copy adds a second IOSurface allocation. Gate is `AppConfig.midDepthHz = 5` (AppConfig.swift:116). The copy is then handed to `VNImageRequestHandler` (173) with `imageCropAndScaleOption = .scaleFill` (170), which downscales it to the Depth Anything V2 Small input (~518x518) — every byte above that resolution is copied only to be discarded. The fit itself (276-365) samples `relative` and `lidar` on a normalized 28x20 grid (309-332), so it is resolution-agnostic.
findings.harm: Per invocation on the main thread: ~4.15 MB memcpy (~0.4-0.9 ms) + two unpooled IOSurface creations (each a kernel round trip, ~0.3-1.0 ms) + first-touch faults across ~4.3 MB of fresh mapping (~0.3-0.8 ms) = roughly 1.3-3.7 ms, five times a second, sustained ~21 MB/s of IOSurface allocate/free churn. On a 30 fps cap the frame budget is 33.3 ms and the BRIEF bar is >=30 fps — the cap equals the bar, so there is no headroom to absorb a 2-4 ms main-thread spike landing on one frame in six. The gate (`renderPath == .pedestrian && !thermalSerious && powerTier == .full` and a drop between 4 m and `midDepthLiDARBandMax * midDepthSupportMargin` = 5 m, GeoARSessionManager.swift:2269-2277) is narrow, so this is not a 10-minute thermal story — but the 4-5 m band is precisely the walk-up-to-the-drop moment, i.e. the product's money moment, and that is where the micro-stutter lands.
findings.fix: Replace `copyPixelBuffer` at the call site with a pooled downscaler: one `CVPixelBufferPool` sized to the model input (e.g. 518x518 or 392x392) plus a `vImageScale_*` / `vImageConvert_420Yp8_CbCr8ToARGB` into the pooled buffer. That removes the per-call IOSurface allocation entirely and cuts the copied bytes by ~20x, taking the main-thread cost to roughly 0.1-0.3 ms with no loss of model input fidelity. Keep the LiDAR copy (196 KB) but pool it too. Keep `copyPixelBuffer` as the general helper — it is correct — just stop calling it at full camera resolution on the main thread. The same pooled downscaler is the fix for RENDER-6, so build it once.

findings.title: PersonSentinel's deliberate no-copy hold is on a .utility queue — the QoS the system throttles hardest under exactly the thermal pressure that stresses the capture pool
findings.trace: The charter asks for judgment on this trade. Verified facts: `update(pixelBuffer:hz:)` (28) takes ARKit's `frame.capturedImage` by reference from GeoARSessionManager.swift:2249 and captures it in the `queue.async` closure (38-68); the buffer is released only when that closure returns, after `handler.perform([request])` (62). The `busy` flag (30-36, 40-44) does correctly bound this to ONE buffer at a time — that half of the build's justification holds. The queue is `DispatchQueue(label: "person-sentinel", qos: .utility)` (13). The build's stated bound is '~10-30 ms hold'; that number is the Vision inference time, not the hold. The hold is queue-hop latency + inference, and `.utility` is the QoS libdispatch is slowest to service under CPU saturation and the one the system deliberately deprioritizes when the device is hot. The asymmetry is backwards: MidFieldDepthEstimator, which now COPIES, runs on `.userInitiated` (MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:86); the sentinel, which does NOT copy, runs on the queue most likely to be starved. Note also the sentinel is fed full-resolution 1920x1440 for a human-rectangle detector that needs nothing like that.
findings.harm: At minute 8 of a walk with the ANE running Depth Anything at 5 Hz, the GPU running the matte compute, and the main thread running frameUpdate plus SwiftUI, a `.utility` work item can wait hundreds of milliseconds before it starts. During that entire wait one ARKit capture IOSurface is pinned. At 2 Hz a 400 ms hold means one pool slot is occupied ~80% of the time — and it grows precisely as the device heats, i.e. compounding with RENDER-3's detached-state pin and with ARKit's own pool pressure. Symptom is ARP-12's: dropped ARFrames and an fps sawtooth that is indistinguishable from thermal throttling in the FT-28/FT-31 traces, which is what makes the heat instrumentation unable to tell the team which problem it is looking at.
findings.fix: Feed the sentinel the same pooled downscaled buffer built for RENDER-5 (a ~512x384 luma or BGRA buffer is more than enough for `VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` with `upperBodyOnly`), so the copy costs ~30-50 us and ARKit's buffer is released before `update` returns. If the copy is rejected, at minimum raise the queue to `.userInitiated` to match the estimator and add an assertion/metric on hold duration so the 'bounded' claim is measured rather than asserted.

findings.title: The first of ARP-12's three named bail paths still holds wrappers to the next encode and never flushes
findings.trace: ARP-12 named three bail-out paths by line. The build fixed two: the semantics/person/mid guard now does `inFlightTextures.removeAll(); CVMetalTextureCacheFlush(textureCache, 0)` before blitting (289-290), and the matteTextures guard does the same (299-300). The first one it named — the compound guard at 229-239 — still falls through to `blit(context: context); return` (237-238) with neither call. Wrappers created inside that guard's own conditions therefore survive to the next encode's `removeAll()` at 226. Ordering means most causes leak nothing (a nil `pipeline`, nil `textureCache`, nil dummies or nil `session?.currentFrame` all short-circuit before any `makeTexture` runs), so the reachable case is narrow: `yTexture` succeeds at 234 and `cbcrTexture` fails at 235 — which is what `CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage` does under memory pressure (kCVReturnAllocationFailed).
findings.harm: One ARKit capture IOSurface stays pinned for an extra frame (~33 ms at the 30 fps cap) — negligible on its own. The case that matters is memory pressure at minute 8-10, which is both when plane-1 wrapping is most likely to fail AND when the capture pool is least able to spare a slot; and if the governor detaches on that same tick (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1144), RENDER-3 applies and the wrapper is pinned until the next attach, which can be minutes.
findings.fix: Route all four exits through one helper — `private func bailOut(_ context: ARView.PostProcessContext) { inFlightTextures.removeAll(); if let textureCache { CVMetalTextureCacheFlush(textureCache, 0) }; blit(context: context) }` — and call it at 237, 289-291 and 299-301 so no future bail path can be added without the release.

findings.title: The ARP-12 copy test covers only the branch production never takes
findings.trace: `PixelBufferCopyTests.testCopyIsContentIdenticalAndIndependent` (193-226) builds an 8x4 `kCVPixelFormatType_DepthFloat32` buffer with nil attributes (197-199). That is non-planar, so it exercises only the `else` branch at MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:237-250; at 8x4 with matching creation paths `srcStride == dstStride`, so only the single-memcpy fast path at 242-243 runs. The multi-plane loop at 221-236 — the branch that actually handles `frame.capturedImage` at 1920x1440 4:2:0 biplanar, which is the entire point of the ARP-12 fix — has zero coverage, as does the `min(srcStride, dstStride)` per-row path at 231-234 and 245-248. The helper is correct as written (I verified the bounds arithmetic on both branches), so this is a coverage gap rather than a live bug — but the untested branch is the one carrying the camera image, and Wave C's binding rule 6 requires doubles to reproduce production's modes.
findings.harm: A future change to plane handling — a new capture format, an alignment tweak, or someone 'simplifying' `min` to one of the strides — copies out-of-bounds or produces a torn CbCr plane, and the suite stays green. A torn chroma plane in the depth model's input degrades the fit silently (`fitInverseDepth` would still return a plausible-looking a/b) rather than failing loudly, so it would surface as 'mid-field occlusion got worse' with no test pointing at the cause.
findings.fix: Add a planar case: create a 1920x1440 `kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarFullRange` source with a deliberately over-aligned stride (`kCVPixelBufferBytesPerRowAlignmentKey: 256`) so `srcStride != dstStride`, fill both planes with a per-pixel deterministic pattern, copy, and assert plane count, both planes' full contents, and independence after mutating the source. Prove non-vacuity by seeded mutation: flip `min(srcStride, dstStride)` to `max` at 231/245 and confirm the test goes red (it will over-read the source row).

testCases.name: testAttachDetachPolicyEnforcesMinimumDwell
testCases.asserts: Extract the pass attach/detach decision at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1139-1148 into a pure `nonisolated static func passAttachment(passNeeded: Bool, attachedSince: Date?, idleSince: Date?, now: Date) -> PassAction` returning .attach/.detach/.hold, then table-test that no input sequence can produce two slot mutations closer together than `AppConfig.passMinDwellSeconds`, including the adversarial sequence needed/idle/needed/idle at 6 s spacing.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails against today's policy: the current code attaches immediately whenever `passNeeded` (1141) and detaches after 5 s idle (1143), so a person stepping in and out on a ~6 s cadence produces an unbounded stream of renderCallbacks stores with no dwell floor. The test cannot pass until a dwell floor exists, which is the exposure-reduction half of the fix.

testCases.name: testRenderCallbackToggleUnderLiveRenderIsRaceFree
testCases.asserts: Device XCTest, built with Thread Sanitizer and SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=complete. Stand up a real ARView with a running session and an installed SemanticOcclusionPass; from the main thread call `setCallbacksActive` alternating true/false at 30 Hz for 60 s (1800 toggles) while the render loop runs at 30 fps. Assert: zero TSan reports naming SemanticOcclusionPass or the renderCallbacks storage, zero crashes, and (as a liveness check) that the frame counter advanced monotonically for the whole run.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails while the defect exists in either of two ways: TSan flags the unsynchronized store at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:170-178 against RealityKit's render-thread load, or the run terminates with EXC_BAD_ACCESS in the render thread. Vacuity proof: replace the toggle with install-once + a locked flag check inside encode and the same harness runs clean; restore the toggle and the report returns. Run it 20x — a single clean run proves nothing, which is exactly why the 130/130 device suite did not catch this.

testCases.name: testMatteHistorySeedSurvivesNaNInPreviousMatte
testCases.asserts: Device Metal unit test. Allocate a 4x4 r16Float texture, fill it with the half NaN bit pattern 0x7E00 via a staging MTLBuffer copy, bind it as previousMatte (index 7), bind a 4x4 destination as nextMatte (index 8), and dispatch `semanticMatte` with uniforms forcing personEnabled=1 and a stencil/scene-depth pair that yields matte=1.0. Read nextMatte back and assert every texel is finite and within [0,1]; read targetColor and assert the camera-restore path fired (color differs from sourceColor).
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today for both assertions: `mix(NaN, 1.0, attackAlpha)` at SemanticMatte.metal:237 yields NaN, so nextMatte is NaN (not in [0,1]), and `if (smoothed > 0.01)` at 240 is false for NaN, so targetColor is an unmodified copy of sourceColor. Vacuity proof: add the `historyValid` uniform gate and the test passes; delete the gate and it fails again. Add the Inf variant (0x7C00) as a second case — it fails at the [0,1] assertion via the `half(smoothed)` saturation at 249.

testCases.name: testResizeReallocatesMatteWithDefinedHistory
testCases.asserts: Drive `encode` twice through a seam with two different `targetColorTexture` sizes (mirroring the ARView(frame:.zero) -> laid-out transition at ARSessionHolder.swift:48/97 and the fullScreenCover animation), and assert that the first encode after each reallocation reports historyValid == 0 in the uniforms it writes (capture uniforms via an injected recorder).
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today because no such flag exists and `ensureMatteTextures` (433-451) publishes uninitialized textures with no signal that the history is invalid. This is the CI-runnable companion to the Metal test above — it pins that the reallocation path, not just the NaN case, is covered.

testCases.name: testDetachFlushesCacheAndReleasesWrappers
testCases.asserts: Inject a `flush: (CVMetalTextureCache) -> Void` seam into SemanticOcclusionPass (Wave C rule 6: the double reproduces production's call, not a stand-in). Drive one successful encode so `inFlightTextures` is populated on a bail path, then call `setCallbacksActive(false)`. Assert the flush seam was invoked exactly once and `inFlightTextures.isEmpty`. Repeat for `uninstall()`.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today with flushCount == 0 for both calls: `setCallbacksActive` (163-180) and `uninstall` (182-191) contain no flush and never touch `inFlightTextures`. Vacuity proof: add `releaseCaptureResources()` to both and the counts become 1; remove it and they return to 0.

testCases.name: testDetachedPassDoesNotPinCaptureSurfaces
testCases.asserts: Device test. Run 300 frames with the pass attached, record the set of IOSurface IDs the texture cache wrapped, then detach and idle 60 s with the camera session still running. Assert that within 2 s of detach every recorded IOSurface's use count returns to its pre-attach baseline, and that the ARFrame timestamp deltas over the idle period show no interval exceeding 2x the nominal frame period.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today: the cache retains its entries indefinitely after detach because no flush runs once `encode` stops, so use counts stay elevated for the whole 60 s and the timestamp trace shows the sawtooth ARP-12 predicted. This is the field-symptom test that distinguishes pool pressure from thermal throttling — the ambiguity ARP-12 called out in the FT-28/FT-31 instrumentation.

testCases.name: testPipelineBuildDoesNotBlockMainActorCallers
testCases.asserts: Inject a `pipelineBuilder: (MTLDevice) -> MTLComputePipelineState?` seam whose double sleeps 200 ms (Wave C rule 6 requires the double to reproduce production's SUSPENSION, not just its return value). Call `prepare(device:)` on a background thread; from the main thread, 10 ms later, measure the wall time of `setCallbacksActive(true)`. Assert < 5 ms.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today measuring ~190 ms, because the builder runs inside the `stateLock` held from SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:194 through 209 and `setCallbacksActive` acquires the same lock at 164 before any short-circuit. Vacuity proof: hoist the build outside the lock (publish-under-lock only) and the measurement drops to microseconds; put it back and the 200 ms returns. Add the same shape for `ensureMatteTextures` with a slow texture-allocator double.

testCases.name: testInferenceInputIsPooledAndDownscaled
testCases.asserts: Call the replacement `prepareInferenceInput(from:)` 100 times with a 1920x1440 biplanar source. Assert (a) the returned buffer's dimensions are <= the model input on both axes, (b) the number of DISTINCT IOSurface identities across the 100 calls is <= the pool depth (recycling, not allocating), and (c) an XCTClockMetric over the 100 calls stays under a 30 ms total budget.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today on all three against `copyPixelBuffer` as called at MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:151: it returns full 1920x1440, yields 100 distinct IOSurfaces (a fresh CVPixelBufferCreate per call at 211-213, no pool exists in the file), and blows the budget at ~1.3-3.7 ms per call. Vacuity proof: the assertions are individually falsifiable — remove the pool and (b) fails; remove the downscale and (a) and (c) fail.

testCases.name: testMidDepthUpdateMainThreadCostBudget
testCases.asserts: Device test with XCTClockMetric measuring `midDepth.update(frame:hz:)` on the main thread only (the synchronous prefix before the queue.async at line 158), fed a real 1920x1440 ARFrame. Assert the main-thread portion is under 0.5 ms — a budget derived from the 33.3 ms frame at targetFrameRate=30 and the fact that the BRIEF's >=30 fps bar leaves zero headroom above the cap.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today at ~1.3-3.7 ms because both copies (151-152) execute before the hop. Vacuity proof: the pooled downscaler brings it under budget; reverting to the full-resolution unpooled copy fails it again. This test is the one that keeps a future 'just copy it, copying is the correct fix' change honest about where the copy runs and how big it is.

testCases.name: testSentinelReleasesCaptureBufferBeforeInferenceCompletes
testCases.asserts: Inject the Vision perform step behind a seam whose double blocks on a semaphore for 500 ms (reproducing production's suspension under a starved .utility queue). Create a source CVPixelBuffer, note its IOSurface use count, pass it to `PersonSentinel.update`, drop the caller's strong reference, and assert the use count returns to baseline BEFORE the semaphore is signalled.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today by construction: the buffer is captured by the queue.async closure at PersonSentinel.swift:38 and released only when the closure returns at 68, so the use count stays elevated for the full 500 ms. Vacuity proof: feed the sentinel a pooled downscaled copy and the count drops immediately; revert to the raw capturedImage and it stays pinned. A second case asserting the same under `qos: .utility` with the CPU saturated by N spinning threads measures the hop latency the 'bounded 10-30 ms' claim omits.

testCases.name: testEveryEncodeBailPathReleasesWrappersAndFlushes
testCases.asserts: Parameterize the encode bail cause over a seam — nil pipeline, nil currentFrame, plane-0-succeeds-plane-1-fails, all-occluders-disabled, matteTextures.count != 2 — and after each assert `inFlightTextures.isEmpty` and flushCount == 1.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today only on the plane-1-failure case, which exits via the blit at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:237 with the plane-0 wrapper still in the array and flushCount == 0. The other four already pass — which is precisely the point: the test names the one path the build missed and pins all four exits so a fifth cannot be added without the release. Vacuity proof: route all exits through the `bailOut` helper and the parameterized case goes green; delete the helper call at 237 and it goes red again.

testCases.name: testCopyPixelBufferPlanarWithStrideMismatch
testCases.asserts: Create a 1920x1440 kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarFullRange source with kCVPixelBufferBytesPerRowAlignmentKey: 256 so srcStride != dstStride, fill Y and CbCr with distinct deterministic per-pixel patterns, copy, and assert plane count == 2, every texel of BOTH planes matches, and mutating the source afterwards does not change the copy.
testCases.failsWhen: Passes today (the helper is correct) — so non-vacuity must be shown by seeded mutation: change `min(srcStride, dstStride)` to `max` at MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:231 and the test must go red with an over-read/corrupt tail on the dst>src case; change `CVPixelBufferGetHeightOfPlane(source, plane)` at 227 to `CVPixelBufferGetHeight(source)` and the CbCr plane assertion must go red. Both mutations survive the current suite untouched, which is the gap this closes.

cleanAreas: CVMetalTextureCacheFlush semantics vs the retained wrapper array (the lens's explicit question) — VERIFIED CORRECT. The flush at SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:391 does NOT invalidate this frame's in-flight wrappers: `retained` (382) holds a +1 CFRetain on every CVMetalTexture and Flush only recycles cache entries with no external reference, so the wrappers survive until the completion handler (384-386) releases them. Placing the flush before RealityKit commits the command buffer is likewise safe. Belt-and-braces confirmed: Metal independently retains textures bound to a command encoder for the command buffer's lifetime, so even a premature CVMetalTexture release could not corrupt the sampled textures.

Matte double-buffer lifetime across reallocation — SAFE. `ensureMatteTextures` (433-451) can release the previous pair while the prior frame's command buffer is still executing, but Metal retains encoder-bound resources (bound at 366-367) until that buffer completes, so there is no use-after-free. (The CONTENTS of the new pair are the RENDER-2 defect; the lifetime is fine.)

stateLock re-entrancy and lock ordering — SAFE today. NSLock is non-recursive and `uninstall` (183) calls `setCallbacksActive`, which fully releases at 167 before `uninstall` re-acquires at 187 — no self-deadlock. `encode` nests stateLock -> SemanticFeed.lock (242) and stateLock -> MidFieldDepthFeed.lock (267); no path takes a feed lock then stateLock (SemanticFeed.update/setEnabled are called only from GeospatialEngine.swift:190/240 and GeoARSessionManager.swift:396/2304, none of which re-enter the pass; MidFieldDepthFeed.publish is called only from the midfield worker at MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:181), so no inversion exists. Flagged only because the line-64 comment misdescribes it.

copyPixelBuffer bounds arithmetic — CORRECT on both branches. Planar (221-236) sizes the copy from the SOURCE plane geometry with `min(srcStride, dstStride)` per row on the mismatch path, which stays in bounds in both directions; the equal-stride fast path copies exactly stride*planeHeight from the plane base, which is the plane's own allocation. Non-planar (237-250) is the same shape. Format/attribute handling is adequate for both ARKit inputs (420YpCbCr8BiPlanarFullRange and DepthFloat32). The defect is cost and coverage, not correctness.

Mid-field pipeline orientation consistency — CONSISTENT. `VNImageRequestHandler` is constructed without an orientation at line 173 (unlike PersonSentinel's `.right` at PersonSentinel.swift:60), but the model output, the LiDAR reference sampled by `fitInverseDepth` (309-332), and the shader's `captureUV` sampling of midDepthTex (SemanticMatte.metal:210) are all in the same sensor frame, so the pipeline is self-consistent. Whether an upright-trained depth model should see a sideways scene is a perception/MATH question, pre-existing and unchanged by Wave D — out of scope per D5.

Per-frame texture re-wrapping cost introduced by the flush — CONSIDERED AND REJECTED as a finding. The per-frame flush can force `CVMetalTextureCacheCreateTextureFromImage` (462-464) to miss on up to 7 buffers per frame, but at steady state the GPU runs 1-2 frames behind, so most entries are still externally referenced at flush time and survive to be recycled. Worst case is ~1% of a render-thread core, and once-per-frame flush after encoding is Apple's own documented idiom. Not a defect.

ARP-7's threading split — CORRECT. `makeMeshDescriptor` is nonisolated static (GeospatialEngine.swift:494) and `MeshResource.generate` (451) run on meshQueue; ModelEntity construction and scene-graph mutation hop back via Task { @MainActor } (453-467); `meshBuildsInFlight` is touched only on the main actor (442, 455). Resource-creation-off-main / scene-mutation-on-main is the correct RealityKit contract. The stale-landing-after-stop() hole is unreachable (stop() is only called from the dead detach()), and `ensureOccluderRoot` re-enabling occluders during transit is pre-existing and identical in the pre-Wave-D synchronous path — both out of scope per D5.

pickVideoFormat (ARP-6) — CORRECT and pure (GeoARSessionManager.swift:687-707), with the UNCAPPED marker and error log on the unsatisfiable branch (668-678). Verified only because it determines the capturedImage size that RENDER-5's cost depends on.

ReactionService re-attach idempotence (SWE-10 remainder) — CORRECT. `listenToMySharedDrops` creates listeners only where `listeners[key] == nil` (ReactionService.swift:130), so the `.active` re-attach at RootView.swift:204 cannot stack duplicates across repeated inactive/active transitions, and `.inactive` correctly falls through to `default: break` (206) so an app-switcher peek does not tear down live streams.

findings.title: perceptionPlan requests .sceneDepth for a mid-field consumer whose serviceable band is 4-5 m — the request predicate is unbounded above and carries no thermal term, so the 60 Hz depth ML fusion runs with zero consumer in the ordinary walk-up scene
findings.trace: Plan depth term (1184-1187): `(midFieldEnabled && anyContentBeyondMidMin && fullTier && pedestrian)`. `anyContentBeyondMidMin` is computed at 1049-1051 as `distance > AppConfig.midDepthMinContentDistance` (= 4 m, AppConfig.swift:118) with NO upper bound. The only consumer of .sceneDepth on that leg is frameUpdate 2269-2277: `maxServiceable = midDepthLiDARBandMax (4.0, AppConfig.swift:137) * midDepthSupportMargin (1.25, AppConfig.swift:131)` = 5.0 m, and `useful` additionally requires `!thermalSerious`. MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:348-354 hard-caps any published fit at `depthMax * 1.25` with `depthMax < 4.0`, so the estimator is structurally incapable of matting content past 5 m. Requested via setPerception:748-758 → makeConfiguration:628-631 inserts .sceneDepth. PowerGovernor.swift:70-76 documents that .serious does NOT demote the tier, so tier stays .full at thermal .serious while the consumer has already shed itself. This is the same request-outlives-use shape the item claims closed (comment at 1157-1160 asserts 'every request derives from the same predicate as its use').
findings.harm: Device: any LiDAR iPhone, pedestrian, camera visible, one drop rendered 10 m ahead and in view (tier .full per PowerGovernor.swift:62-64), no person in frame (personLikely false → plan.person false). plan.depth resolves true from the mid-field term alone; ARKit's scene-depth ML fusion is requested and runs at its fixed internal 60 Hz for the entire session while `useful` at 2271-2277 is false on every single frame, so midDepth.update is never called and midDepth.feed.invalidate() (2283-2285) is the only thing that ever executes. Pure heat with zero rendered benefit — ADR-033's premise ('every expensive subsystem runs only while the scene needs it') inverted. It compounds at thermal .serious: the mid-field consumer disables itself on `!thermalSerious` while the plan keeps requesting the stream, so the app burns the hottest ARKit depth path hardest exactly when it is already losing the NOT-thermal-.serious-at-10-min bar. Because 4-5 m is a band a walk-up drop crosses in about two seconds and 2 km is the visibility radius (AppConfig.swift:159), the leaking case is the normal case, not the corner.
findings.fix: Give the plan the consumer's real predicate. Replace `anyContentBeyondMidMin: Bool` with `midFieldServiceable: Bool` computed in updatePowerTier from the SAME expression frameUpdate uses (`d > midDepthMinContentDistance && d < midDepthLiDARBandMax * midDepthSupportMargin`), and add `thermalSerious: Bool` to the signature so the depth term reads `... && midFieldServiceable && fullTier && pedestrian && !thermalSerious`. Then extract the consumer side as `nonisolated static func midFieldUseful(distances:pedestrian:thermalSerious:fullTier:) -> Bool` and have frameUpdate:2271 call it, so a single pure function is provably the request AND the use — the coupling then has a test that cannot drift.

findings.title: resumeSession rebuilds from a stale appliedPerception while the Wave-D hysteresis timers survive the suspend, firing a second session.run milliseconds after the resume run — a double reconfiguration at the ADR-043 reveal moment
findings.trace: suspendSession (402-414) pauses the session and cancels the tick but does not touch `appliedPerception` (747) or `personDownSince`/`depthDownSince` (1151-1152). ARSessionHolder.swift:68-72 sets cameraVisible=false at tab-leave, then 109-119 waits pauseGraceSeconds (5 s, AppConfig.swift:150) before suspend — so the last tick before suspend already ran the plan with cameraVisible=false: person/depth desired false, hysteresis (1195-1215) sets downSince=now and RETURNS TRUE, so appliedPerception is frozen at (reconstruction:false, person:true, depth:true) whenever a person was in frame at tab-leave. On return, ARSessionHolder.swift:61-66 calls resumeSession then markCameraVisible, both synchronously; resumeSession:450-454 runs `makeConfiguration(reconstruction: false, personSeg: true, sceneDepth: true)` from that frozen tuple and calls startTicking (461). startTicking:931-939 executes tick() on its FIRST iteration with no sleep. PersonSentinel.swift:21-24 decays personLikely purely on wall clock (<5 s), so after any suspension longer than 5 s it is false; hysteresis at 1206-1210 then sees a downSince minutes old, returns false immediately, and setPerception:748-758 fires a SECOND `arView.session.run(...)` for (true,false,false). Neither run updates `sessionRunSince` — only resumeSession:459 does — so the ADR-043 gate at 2220-2226 measures against the first run only.
findings.harm: Device: user leaves the camera tab with someone in frame, returns 30 s later. ARKit receives two `run(config)` calls a few milliseconds apart, each restarting the capture pipeline and relocalization against the retained world map. A frame from the first run's brief life satisfies `frame.timestamp > sessionRunSince` and flips sessionFrameReady true, so the reveal overlay (capped at 1.6 s, AppConfig.swift:154) dismisses onto the second reconfiguration's stall — the user is shown a black or frozen viewfinder at the exact instant killer #1 is measured. Secondary: the resume run requests .personSegmentation (14-29 ms/frame) and .sceneDepth for a scene that wants neither, and requests NO reconstruction for a pedestrian scene that does, so the first second after every tab-return has the perception diet exactly inverted. This is Wave-D-introduced: the pre-Wave-D build had no hysteresis (verified — `downSince` does not appear in commit 2a0f146's GeoARSessionManager.swift), so the frozen appliedPerception could not be a lie about what the plan currently wants.
findings.fix: Make suspend a real reset of the scheduler: in suspendSession, clear `personDownSince`/`depthDownSince` and set `appliedPerception = (false,false,false)` (the session is paused; nothing is applied). Then have resumeSession compute the plan ONCE for the current scene and run THAT config, rather than replaying a tuple captured 5 s into a tab-flip. Additionally, set `sessionRunSince = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime` inside setPerception:752 so the ADR-043 reveal gate cannot be satisfied by a frame that predates a reconfiguration. Structurally: lift the applied-tuple + hold timers into a `PerceptionScheduler` value type with explicit `suspend()`/`resume(plan:)` transitions so the state cannot outlive the session it describes.

findings.title: Wave D turned occlusionActive from a static capability into live state but left setWindowMode's re-insert guarded on it — exiting GLASS mode while reconstruction is shed drops .occlusion from sceneUnderstanding permanently for the rest of the session
findings.trace: `occlusionActive` is now live state: declared 75, forced false in runGPSCompass:726, and assigned `= appliedPerception.reconstruction` in updatePowerTier:1119. The ONLY writers of `arView.environment.sceneUnderstanding.options` are runGPSCompass:719-722 (cold run), applyRenderPathIfNeeded:1364 / 1372-1375 (transit/pedestrian, correctly re-keyed to device capability by Wave D), and setWindowMode:1029 / 1032-1034. setWindowMode's restore still reads `guard occlusionActive` — which under Wave D can be false. In commit 2a0f146 the same line read the same way but occlusionActive was `= occlusionCapable`, a static device fact (old line 678), so the restore was unconditional on capable hardware. Deterministic trigger: reconstruction is shed at thermal .critical (1178 `!thermalCritical`), which destroys the mesh; updateWindowMode:1005-1010 then raycasts `.sceneUnderstanding` against nothing, `hit` is nil, `blockedNear` false (1010), windowCounterEvidence reaches 6 in ~2.4 s (1016-1019) and setWindowMode(false) runs while occlusionActive is false. Nothing re-inserts .occlusion when reconstruction later returns: updatePowerTier:1119 only writes the flag, never the option set.
findings.harm: Device: LiDAR iPhone, pedestrian, viewing a far drop through a window (GLASS chip lit per ARScreen.swift:389-391), phone reaches thermal .critical after ~10 min. Within 2.4 s of the mesh disappearing, window mode exits and .occlusion is dropped from sceneUnderstanding without being restored. When thermal recovers to .fair, the plan re-requests reconstruction, appliedPerception.reconstruction goes true, `occlusionActive` goes true and ARScreen.swift:372-374 lights the blue LiDAR chip — while RealityKit is no longer occluding against the reconstructed mesh at all. Every drop now draws through walls, cars and the floor for the remainder of the session, directly violating the BRIEF's zero-draw-over-known-front-surface bar, and the HUD instrument the counsel relies on for field evidence actively asserts the opposite. Only a cold restart (runGPSCompass) or a transit→pedestrian round trip recovers it, neither of which the user has any way to trigger deliberately.
findings.fix: Stop treating the sceneUnderstanding option set as event-driven. Add `nonisolated static func occlusionOptionDesired(capable:reconstructionApplied:pedestrian:windowModeActive:) -> Bool` and apply it once per tick at the end of updatePowerTier (insert/remove to match), exactly as Wave C's ARP-3 ruling required for semanticMatteArmed ('derived state is computed from its inputs each tick, never written inside the branch its own precondition guards' — the comment at 2288-2294 states the rule this site violates). setWindowMode and applyRenderPathIfNeeded then only set their own flags; neither touches options.

findings.title: Reconstruction is the one perception axis with no hysteresis, and cameraVisible is a term of it — every tab flip inside the pre-warm grace destroys and rebuilds the LiDAR mesh while sceneUnderstanding still requests occlusion
findings.trace: 1178: `reconstruction = cameraVisible && pedestrian && !thermalCritical`. applyPerceptionHysteresis is applied to person (1108-1111) and depth (1112-1115) only; the reconstruction term is passed raw into setPerception at 1116. ARSessionHolder.swift:68-72 calls markCameraHidden() the moment the camera view disappears (GeoARSessionManager.swift:466-468 sets cameraVisible=false) but only schedules the pause 5 s later (ARSessionHolder.swift:109-119); suspendSession is what cancels the tick (408-409), so for those 5 s the tick keeps running and the very next iteration (≤400 ms) reaches 1116 with reconstruction=false and fires session.run on a session the user is walking away from. makeConfiguration:622-624 then omits sceneReconstruction, which discards the accumulated mesh. Nothing removes `.occlusion` from sceneUnderstanding across this window (only setWindowMode:1029 and the transit branch:1364 ever do). On return, tick raises it again → a third session.run and a mesh rebuild from zero. The item's own rationale at 615-621 names this exact harm ('every re-enable rebuilds the mesh from nothing, leaving a multi-second occlusion hole while sceneUnderstanding still requests occlusion') and the tests only cover the tier/presence axis (WaveDTests.swift:106-113), never the visibility axis.
findings.harm: Device: LiDAR iPhone, drops placed, user flips Camera→Map→Camera in under 5 s (the flow ADR-013/ADR-043's grace window exists to make free). Sequence observed in code: run(no-recon) at tab-leave, run(recon) at tab-return, with the mesh dropped in between. On return the user is looking at a scene whose reconstruction is rebuilding from nothing over several seconds while `.occlusion` is still in the sceneUnderstanding option set — content draws over the wall and the parked car for the whole rebuild, which is the SWE-11 harm verbatim, on the most frequent navigation in the app. Each flip also costs two full ARSession reconfigurations (tracking hitch, fps dip) at a moment the user is looking at the screen.
findings.fix: Add a visibility grace to the stable axis: keep `lastCameraVisibleAt` and pass `cameraRecentlyVisible = Date().timeIntervalSince(lastCameraVisibleAt) < AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds` into perceptionPlan in place of raw `cameraVisible` for the reconstruction term only (person/depth must keep the hard visibility term — they are per-frame ML and the plan's totality property at 1174-1177 depends on it). Simplest equivalent: guard setPerception on `cameraVisible || tickTask == nil` so no reconfiguration happens during the grace at all, letting suspendSession's pause be the shed. Either way reconstruction must not change state on a transition the app has already decided to smooth over.

findings.title: The capture-format policy has no resolution-only fallback: on a device with no format at or below the target fps it returns nil and lets ARKit's default (the highest-throughput format) stand, abandoning the resolution lever ADR-030 calls the biggest heat control
findings.trace: pickVideoFormat:696 `guard format.fps <= targetFPS, area >= minArea, area <= maxArea else { continue }` — fps is a hard filter with no second pass, so `best` stays nil (707) when every in-band format is 60 fps. makeConfiguration:668-679 then reads `config.videoFormat` unchanged (ARKit documents the default as `supportedVideoFormats.first`, the device's recommended/highest-throughput entry) and only marks the HUD string UNCAPPED. The repo's own fixture asserts this device class is real: WaveDTests.swift:20-30 `testNeverSelects4KEvenWhenItIsTheOnly30FPSFormat` describes 'the ADR-034 regression device' whose only sub-target format is out-of-band 4K — on that device the picker refuses everything, including the perfectly good 1280×720@60 that would be in the list. AppConfig.swift:86 targetFrameRate = 30. Secondary defect at the same site: makeConfiguration re-runs the whole scan and rewrites the @Published `videoFormatDescription` (662-666) on EVERY setPerception call, so the UNCAPPED metricsLog.error at 678 repeats on every perception change and the HUD invalidates each time.
findings.harm: Device: any iPhone whose ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportedVideoFormats offers no entry with fps ≤ 30 inside [1280×720 … 1920×1440]. The app runs the platform default — typically 1920×1440@60 — instead of the 1280×720@60 that is sitting unselected in the same list: ~2.25× the pixels through the ISP and through every downstream ARKit ML stage (person segmentation, scene depth fusion, the app's own Metal pass and Vision sentinel), at identical frame rate. ADR-030 states capture is the single biggest heat lever; the policy declines to pull it in exactly the case where the fps half of the lever is unavailable. Sustained over the 10-minute NOT-thermal-.serious bar this is the difference between passing and not, and the only signal is a HUD suffix the field tester has to notice.
findings.fix: Make the policy two-stage inside pickVideoFormat: first pass unchanged (highest fps ≤ target, then smallest area). If nil, second pass over the same area bounds selecting LOWEST fps then SMALLEST area, and return that index with a distinct marker so the HUD can read 'FPS-UNCAPPED' rather than fully UNCAPPED. Return only nil when no format is in the area band at all. Keep the loud log for both degraded cases. Separately, cache the picked format/description on first computation so setPerception does not rescan and republish per reconfiguration.

findings.title: Consumers of the reconstruction mesh are not gated on the reconstruction request: snapNearestDropToGround silently degrades to a guessed height, then ground-LOCKS and PERSISTS it as if it were a measurement
findings.trace: The plan can shed reconstruction (1178) on three axes: camera hidden, transit, thermal .critical. Two consumers read the mesh unconditionally. (a) snapNearestDropToGround:1883-1892 raycasts `mask: .sceneUnderstanding` as the second rung of its truth chain; with reconstruction shed the mesh anchors and their collision shapes (requested at 722) are gone, the raycast returns nothing and the chain falls through to estimatedGroundY (1896, plane anchors) or `camera.y - 1.65` (1897). The result is then committed with `adjustNearestDrop(height:commit:true)` at 1903 — which reaches library.update(persist: true) at 1826 — and ground-LOCKED at 1905. groundLockBaseY is authoritative forever: it overrides GPS re-sync (1608) and overrides VPS terrain transforms outright (820-822). Nothing records the provenance of the value, so a fabricated height is indistinguishable from a LiDAR measurement. The ARScreen 'Place on ground' button (ARScreen.swift:542-551) is unconditional — no thermal or render-path gate. (b) updateWindowMode:1005-1010 probes the same mesh; with reconstruction shed the probe cannot return a hit, so GLASS mode always resolves to 'off' — which is the deterministic trigger for ARPCFG-3.
findings.harm: Device: LiDAR iPhone at thermal .critical after ~10 min (or in transit, which Wave D newly added as a shedding axis). The user taps 'Place on ground' on a drop 8 m away; there is no mesh, no horizontal plane anchor has resolved at that distance, so the ground is taken as the camera's own height minus 1.65 m — the user's standing plane, not the ground under the drop. The drop snaps to a wrong height, the wrong height is written into groundLockBaseY so every later GPS re-sync and every VPS terrain anchor is forbidden from correcting it, and `persist: true` ships that height to Firestore where every recipient of the shared link renders the drop buried or floating. The failure is silent — the same tap on a cool phone measures correctly — so it reads to the user as the app randomly ignoring 'Place on ground'.
findings.fix: Return provenance from the truth chain: make it `enum GroundEstimate { case planeRaycast(Float), mesh(Float), planeAnchor(Float), assumedEyeHeight(Float) }` computed by a pure `nonisolated static func resolveGround(planeHit:meshHit:planeAnchorY:cameraY:) -> GroundEstimate`. Only the first three set groundLockBaseY and pass `persist: true`; `.assumedEyeHeight` applies the visual move but must not lock and must not persist, and should surface through showPersistError (93) as 'Couldn't find the ground here'. Independently, skip the mesh rung and the window-mode probe entirely when `appliedPerception.reconstruction == false` so the code states its dependency instead of discovering it as an empty result.

findings.title: perceptionPlan carries no hardware-support terms, so appliedPerception records requests makeConfiguration never made — the live-state LiDAR chip lights on non-LiDAR phones and setPerception churns session.run for no-op requests
findings.trace: makeConfiguration guards each request on hardware: reconstruction on `supportsSceneReconstruction(.mesh)` (622) and depth on `supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth)` (628-629). perceptionPlan (1161-1189) has no such terms — it takes `supportsCustomPersonOcclusion` for the person leg only (1185), and the mid-field depth leg (1186) has none at all. setPerception:751 assigns `appliedPerception = desired` BEFORE building the config, so appliedPerception records the desire, not the configuration. On a non-LiDAR iPhone (no mesh, no sceneDepth — the majority of the install base): `appliedPerception.reconstruction` is true whenever the camera is visible and pedestrian, so line 1119 sets `occlusionActive = true` and ARScreen.swift:372-374 lights the blue 'LiDAR' chip — on a phone where runGPSCompass:716-723 never even inserted `.occlusion` because `occlusionCapable` was false. This directly falsifies the item's own claim at 1117-1118 ('the HUD chip reports what is ACTUALLY configured this session, not a static device capability'). Symmetrically, `appliedPerception.depth` toggles as content crosses 4 m or tier changes, and each toggle passes the change-guard at 750 and fires session.run for a config that is byte-identical to the previous one.
findings.harm: Device: iPhone 15 / 16 non-Pro or SE, pedestrian, camera visible. The HUD asserts LiDAR occlusion is active for the whole session on hardware that has no scene reconstruction and no scene depth, so the field instrument the counsel uses to diagnose draw-over reports and heat reports is lying on the majority of shipping devices — a field tester reporting 'content draws over the wall with the LiDAR chip lit' will send the investigation at the Metal pass instead of at the device class. Second harm on the same devices: every crossing of the 4 m mid-field boundary and every .full↔.cruise transition fires a real `arView.session.run(config)` whose configuration is unchanged, costing a tracking reset and a visible fps hitch for a request the platform silently drops.
findings.fix: Pass the two capability booleans into perceptionPlan (`supportsSceneReconstruction`, `supportsSceneDepth`) and AND them into the reconstruction and depth terms respectively, so the plan can only ever desire what the hardware can deliver. That makes appliedPerception a faithful record of the running configuration, makes the change-guard at 750 correct by construction (identical configs produce identical tuples), and makes `occlusionActive` honest without reintroducing the static-capability flag Wave D was right to remove.

testCases.name: testSuspendClearsPerceptionHoldsSoResumeDoesNotImmediatelyReconfigure
testCases.asserts: Extract the applied tuple + hold timers into `struct PerceptionScheduler { mutating func evaluate(plan:, now:) -> (recon,person,depth); mutating func suspend(); func resumeConfig(plan:) -> (recon,person,depth) }` with an injected clock (Wave C rule 6: the double reproduces production's suspension mode, not just its happy path). testCases.name: testOcclusionOptionSurvivesAGlassExitDuringThermalShedding

testCases.name: testReconstructionSurvivesATabFlipInsideThePauseGrace

testCases.name: testFallsBackToSmallestAreaWhenNoFormatMeetsTheFPSCap

testCases.asserts: Against the extracted `resolveGround(planeHit:meshHit:planeAnchorY:cameraY:) -> GroundEstimate` plus a FakeRaycaster double that returns no hits for both the ARKit plane query and the .sceneUnderstanding mesh query (Wave C rule 6: the double reproduces the shed-stream FAILURE mode, not only the success mode): assert the result is `.assumedEyeHeight`, that groundLockBaseY has no entry for the drop afterwards, and that the fake DropLibrary recorded ZERO update(persist: true) calls. testCases.name: testPlanNeverRequestsAStreamTheHardwareCannotProvide
testCases.asserts: With the two capability parameters added to perceptionPlan: `plan(supportsSceneReconstruction: false)` → reconstruction FALSE on every other input combination (camera visible, pedestrian, nominal thermal); `plan(supportsSceneDepth: false, anyContentBeyondMidMin: true, fullTier: true)` → depth FALSE; and a manager-level assertion that after a full updatePowerTier on simulated non-LiDAR capabilities, `occlusionActive == false` so the ARScreen LiDAR chip stays dark.

cleanAreas: perceptionPlan's totality over cameraVisible (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1174-1187): all three terms carry the visibility predicate directly, so the plan never depends on the governor keeping tier and visibility consistent. WaveDTests.swift:130-135 locks it non-vacuously (it also flips tierAboveIdle and personLikely, so it would still catch a regression in the visibility term alone). This is a genuine hardening and the charter's claim that this case caught a real hole during the build is consistent with the code.

The transit legs of ARP-8 are genuinely closed: reconstruction (1178) and the mid-field depth leg (1186) both carry `pedestrian`, so meshing glass at vehicle speed and running LiDAR-aligned neural depth against a vehicle interior are both structurally impossible now. WaveDTests.swift:85-98 covers both directions (transit sheds recon+midfield depth, transit KEEPS person+its depth test) — the pair is discriminating.

pickVideoFormat's mechanics inside its stated policy (687-707): pure and nonisolated, index space maps 1:1 onto the caller's array (654-659), both area bounds are inclusive and correctly oriented (1280×720 exactly at the floor and 1920×1440 exactly at the ceiling are both accepted), the highest-fps-then-smallest-area tie-break is implemented exactly as documented, and portrait/landscape is a non-issue because the comparison is on area. The five table tests are non-vacuous.

The non-custom-person hardware path: plan.depth's person leg is gated on supportsCustomPersonOcclusion (1185) and makeConfiguration falls through to .personSegmentationWithDepth (643-645), so a device without LiDAR never pays for a separate .sceneDepth request on behalf of person occlusion. WaveDTests.swift:122-128 locks it.

Window mode sheds both fast depth consumers (1183 person, 1187 depth) while deliberately keeping reconstruction — correct, because the mesh is what updateWindowMode itself probes to decide when to exit. WaveDTests.swift:115-120 asserts all three.

setPerception's change-guard (750) and its ordering: appliedPerception is written before the run, and runGPSCompass (713-714) sets the idle tuple before its own run, so the recorded state matches the configuration actually run on both cold paths. The mode == .gpsCompass guard keeps the latent Tier B geoTracking path from corrupting the tuple.

applyPerceptionHysteresis (1195-1215) is correct as specified: upgrades are immediate, the `guard applied` early-out (1202-1205) means an already-off stream is never re-raised by the hold, and downSince is cleared on every path that returns a settled value. The defect in ARPCFG-2 is the timer's lifetime across suspend, not this function's logic.

garFeedInterval (1226-1251) still honours its full ladder after the Wave D changes — coverage-negative 1 Hz, the 20 s/60 s convergence sprint, idle-tier clamping and the thermalSerious floor are all intact and unaffected by the new perception axes.

ARP-12's buffer-ownership direction is implemented as the researcher corrected it, and the PersonSentinel non-copy trade is sound in my judgment: the closure retains a single CVPixelBuffer rather than the ARFrame (PersonSentinel.swift:37-40), is serialized by the busy flag (30-35), and at 2 Hz with a ~10-30 ms hold occupies well under a tenth of the capture pool. It is fed only while cameraVisible and content exists (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2248-2250).

reviews.lens: State lifecycle + entanglement (SWE-5 live-edit identity/governor pin, SWE-10 listener lifecycle remainder, ARP-7 streetscape build pipeline). Traced every per-drop collection in GeoARSessionManager against all three destroy-a-drop sites and resetPlacements; traced editingDropID's full write/clear graph; traced the ARScreen slider gesture -> adjustNearestDrop -> DropLibrary.update persistence chain; traced occlusionActive's migration from capability flag to live state and both of its consumers; traced the GeospatialEngine per-drop anchor state and the meshQueue build/teardown pipeline; traced ReactionService listener attach/prime/stop against RootView's scenePhase wiring. Diffed against 2a0f146 (pre-Wave-D) where a Wave D change could have made an existing residual more dangerous.

closureVerdicts.trace: Outside my lens; verified structurally only. SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:65 declares one `stateLock`; encode holds it for its whole CPU body (223-224), prepare(device:) (194-195), uninstall (187-190) and setCallbacksActive (164-167) all take it, and callbacksActive is behind a locked accessor (152-156). No state-lifecycle defect found: the pass is created once in attach() (GeoARSessionManager.swift:357) and uninstall() is only reachable from detach(), which has zero call sites app-wide, so there is no teardown/re-create race to leak.

Outside my lens; no state-lifecycle defect found. MidFieldDepthEstimator.copyPixelBuffer is exercised by WaveDTests.swift PixelBufferCopyTests for content-identity and source-independence; GeoARSessionManager.swift:2283-2285 invalidates the feed when the estimator stops being useful, so no stale sample survives a mode change.
