Five table tests in WaveDTests.swift including the 4K-only-30fps refusal. videoFormatDescription is written on every makeConfiguration call, so it cannot go stale across a perception swap.

The main-thread stall IS gone: makeMeshDescriptor is nonisolated static (GeospatialEngine.swift:494), extraction + MeshResource.generate run on meshQueue (445-452), install hops back to @MainActor (453), generate failures are logged (457), and the stale-landing guard is present (461). But the pipeline is unbounded and self-defeating in exactly the dense-block case it exists for: no cap on enqueued builds, no cancellation, each closure pins a GARStreetscapeGeometry, and the relevance check at 461 runs AFTER the expensive work rather than before it. Teardown does not clear meshBuildsInFlight (426) or lastSeenGeometryIDs (429) — stop() (194-214) and invalidateAllAnchors() (392-402) both skip them. See F9.

perceptionPlan is a pure nonisolated static (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1161-1189), reconstruction keys only on stable session facts (1178), and 7 table tests cover transit/thermal/presence-cycle/camera-hidden. applyPerceptionHysteresis (1195-1215) correctly never re-raises an already-off stream. But the SWE-11 tail — turning occlusionActive from a static capability flag into live state (1119, vs 2a0f146:678 `occlusionActive = occlusionCapable`) — was a HALF migration: consumer #2 at 1372 was correctly re-keyed to device capability, consumer #1 at 1032 still reads the now-live flag and can permanently drop `.occlusion` from sceneUnderstanding. That is a Wave-D-introduced regression inside the item's own change. See F2.

The request side is closed: transit sheds reconstruction and the mid-field depth leg from the same predicate as their use (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1178, 1186), table-tested (testTransitShedsReconstructionAndMidFieldDepth). But F2 recreates the identical 'cost with no consumer' class in the opposite direction: after a window-mode exit taken while reconstruction was momentarily off, `.sceneReconstruction = .mesh` keeps being requested and paid for (622-624) with `.occlusion` absent from sceneUnderstanding.options — full LiDAR meshing watts, zero occlusion, and the HUD chip (ARScreen.swift:372) asserting the opposite.

The timer-driven half is genuinely closed: editingDropID is captured at gesture start (1764), updateNearest is frozen while a drag is live (1418), commit clears the capture (1835), and both removal loops (1662, 2155) route through removePerDropState (1395-1412), which covers all 15 manager-side per-drop collections plus editingDropID. Three failure modes the finding named remain reachable: (1) nothing terminates an unfinished gesture, so editingDropID + liveEditingDrops leak for the session and the governor pin is back (F1); (2) the helper's own vanish-guard (1769-1770) is provably dead code because the nearestDrop fallback at 1768 always matches while the capture is set, and that fallback resurrects deleted drops into the library (F4); (3) clearRoomDrops (554-568) is a third destroy-a-drop's-presence site that was left byte-identical to 2a0f146:547-561 and does not clear the NEW editingDropID field, falsifying removePerDropState's own doc claim at 1390 (F3).

One fullScreenCover(item:) over Destination (RootView.swift:60), compat accessors preserve call sites (AppRouter.swift:46-69), beginFireworksDemo/endFireworksDemo are single destination changes (90-99), MemoryScreen's send-one-back is an explicit endSession + beginCreate with no dismiss race (RootView.swift:81-86), and dismissal side effects are centralized in destinationBinding (20-42). Five router tests pass. Residual: the deep-link queue's promotion is triggered only by a router.destination transition to nil (109-114), so a link queued behind the ReceiveScreen SHEET is stranded when that sheet is dismissed without accepting — destination never moves. See F7.

The mechanism works: RootView.swift:200-209 stops listeners on .background and re-attaches on .active, ReactionService.stop() (217-221) removes every registration and clears primedListeners, and listenToMySharedDrops is idempotent (130). The missing deinit is acceptable for foreground/background on a single-scene iPhone app (one WindowGroup, AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:22) but leaves live Firestore registrations behind if a scene is ever destroyed, since FIRListenerRegistration does not detach on dealloc. The real problem is the payload, not the ownership: clearing primedListeners means the re-attach's initial snapshot is classified as history (153-156), and with `.order(by:"at",descending:true).limit(to:1)` that snapshot IS the reaction that arrived while backgrounded. There is no push channel and no other sender-side surface, so the reaction is lost permanently. See F6.

findings.title: No termination path for an unfinished slider gesture: editingDropID + liveEditingDrops leak for the whole session (governor pinned .full, nearest frozen)
findings.trace: editingDropID is set on the first non-commit tick (1764) and liveEditingDrops gains the id (1782). The complete set of clearers is: commit (1834-1835), removePerDropState for that id (1406-1407), resetPlacements (781-782), clearRoomDrops for liveEditingDrops only (564), and the dead bail at 1769-1770 (see STATE-4). There is no timeout, no cancel path, and no scene-lifecycle clear: suspendSession (402-414) does not touch either, resumeSession (425-462) does not, markCameraHidden (466-468) does not, and detach() (370-387) — the only other resetPlacements caller — has zero call sites app-wide (ARSessionHolder never calls it; `attached` at line 93 is never reset). resetPlacements is therefore reachable only via runGPSCompass on session failure or relocalization give-up. Meanwhile the commit only ever arrives from SwiftUI Slider onEditingChanged(false) (ARScreen.swift:488-492, 509-513, 530-534), which is not delivered when the panel is torn out of the hierarchy mid-gesture. adjustPanel is conditional on `manager.nearestDrop != nil, manager.renderedDropCount > 0, !demoing` (ARScreen.swift:285) and on `!hudHidden` (143), and hudHidden is toggled by a tap recognizer on a SIBLING view (110-118) — a second finger tapping the viewfinder while the thumb drags the slider destroys the panel mid-drag. Backgrounding the app mid-drag is the same shape.
findings.harm: Once leaked: (a) HEAT — PowerGovernor.evaluate takes isLiveEditing (1064 -> PowerGovernor.swift:62) as an unconditional .full trigger, so the moment the camera surface returns the tier is pinned .full for the rest of the session: GAR feed at 15 Hz (1242), reconstruction+person+depth all requested, and the mid-field ANE model unlocked because its gate is `powerTier == .full` (2272). This is precisely the thermal path the BRIEF bar 'NOT thermal .serious at 10 min' forbids, and it is the exact harm SWE-5 was filed for — Wave D moved the trigger from 'nearest changed mid-drag' to 'gesture never ended' without adding a terminator. (b) FUNCTIONAL — updateNearest returns immediately while the capture is set (1418), so nearestDrop is frozen for the session: the guidance card (ARScreen.swift:290-295), the adjust panel, snapNearestDropToGround (1867) and updateWindowMode (989-991) all operate on a drop the user may be a kilometre away from, and no new drop can ever become nearest.
findings.fix: Record `lastLiveEditTickAt` on every non-commit adjustNearestDrop call. In tick(), if editingDropID != nil and Date().timeIntervalSince(lastLiveEditTickAt) > 1.5, abandon the gesture: clear editingDropID and remove the id from liveEditingDrops (do NOT persist — an abandoned gesture is not a commit). Additionally clear both in suspendSession() and markCameraHidden() so a backgrounded drag can never survive into the next foreground. Extract the whole thing as a pure LiveEditRegistry so the expiry policy is table-testable.

findings.title: occlusionActive half-migrated from capability to live state: window-mode exit can permanently drop .occlusion while the mesh keeps being built and the HUD claims LiDAR is on
findings.trace: Pre-Wave-D, occlusionActive was a static device-capability flag set once (2a0f146:678 `occlusionActive = occlusionCapable`) and never falsified, so both of its consumers — applyRenderPathIfNeeded's pedestrian branch (2a0f146:1229) and setWindowMode(false) (2a0f146:978) — were correct capability gates. Wave D redefined it as live state (`occlusionActive = appliedPerception.reconstruction`, line 1119; initialized false at 726) and re-keyed consumer #1 to device capability (1372-1375, with the comment explicitly acknowledging the change) but left consumer #2 at 1032 reading the live flag. Ordering makes it worse: tick() calls updateWindowMode() (967) BEFORE updatePowerTier() (968), so setWindowMode always reads the previous tick's value. Failure sequence: (1) user views a far drop through glass -> windowEvidence reaches 3 -> setWindowMode(true) removes .occlusion (1029). (2) User closes the camera cover -> markCameraHidden -> cameraVisible=false -> perceptionPlan's reconstruction term is `cameraVisible && pedestrian && !thermalCritical` (1178) -> false -> appliedPerception.reconstruction=false -> occlusionActive=false (1119). The tick loop keeps running through pauseGraceSeconds=5 s (ARSessionHolder.swift:109-119, AppConfig pauseGraceSeconds=5). (3) With the phone pocketed, isInView fails (999) -> windowCounterEvidence increments -> at 6 ticks (2.4 s) setWindowMode(false) runs with occlusionActive==false -> the `if occlusionActive` guard at 1032 fails -> .occlusion is NOT re-inserted. (4) Camera reopens: reconstruction returns, occlusionActive=true, HUD lights the LiDAR chip (ARScreen.swift:372), config.sceneReconstruction=.mesh is requested and paid for (622-624). Nothing ever re-inserts .occlusion: the only other writers are runGPSCompass (719, reached only on failure/relocalize-giveup) and an actual transit<->pedestrian edge (1374), and setWindowMode is edge-guarded (1023) so it will not fire again. The same sequence runs on a thermal .critical excursion taken while window mode is active. Also reachable in the reverse order for a device that is thermally critical when the user walks away from the window.
findings.harm: LiDAR scene occlusion is silently and permanently off for the rest of the session while the HUD asserts it is on and the session pays full mesh-reconstruction watts for a consumer that no longer exists. Virtual content draws straight through real walls, doors and parked cars — a direct violation of the BRIEF hard bar 'zero draw-over-known-front-surface frames' — and simultaneously a re-creation of ARP-8's 'expensive request with no consumer' heat class that Wave D closed on the transit axis. Both the correctness bar and the heat bar fail from one line, and the field evidence surface (the LiDAR chip) actively misleads the reporter.
findings.fix: Gate line 1032 on device capability, exactly as 1372 was corrected: `if ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsSceneReconstruction(.mesh) || ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth), renderPath == .pedestrian`. Better: stop edge-toggling sceneUnderstanding.options entirely and re-derive it every tick from the pure predicate `occlusionCapable && pedestrian && !windowModeActive`, applied after updatePowerTier so it never reads a stale sibling. Extract that predicate as a nonisolated static so it is table-testable.

findings.title: clearRoomDrops is still an ad-hoc third destroy site — leaves editingDropID and revealedDrops behind, and can persist a ROOM TEST drop to the cloud
findings.trace: removePerDropState's doc claims 'EVERY site that destroys a drop's presence goes through here' (1390-1394), and both removal loops do (1662, 2155). clearRoomDrops (554-568) does not — it is byte-identical to 2a0f146:547-561, verified by diff, while editingDropID is a field Wave D introduced. Its inline loop clears 8 collections and misses editingDropID and revealedDrops. revealedDrops IS reachable for room drops: frameUpdate iterates `markers` (2322), room drops get a marker in makeHolder (1719-1726), and any holder within 25 m inserts into revealedDrops (2328) — a room drop placed 2.5 m ahead qualifies on the first frame. That is the same unbounded-set growth Wave D fixed for resetPlacements (785). The editingDropID miss is load-bearing: with the capture pointing at a cleared room drop, updateNearest stays frozen (1418) and the next slider tick resolves the target through the nearestDrop fallback (1768) rather than bailing, so placedDrops[id] is re-populated (1778) and — because roomDrops[id] is now nil (566) and demoDrops has no match — the write falls through to the library branch (1818-1831), calling `library.update(edited, persist: commit)`. DropStore.swift:917-923 inserts an absent drop rather than rejecting it, then local.save + enqueueCloudSync.
findings.harm: Clearing the Playground while a slider gesture is unfinished (trivially reachable once STATE-1 has stranded a capture) freezes nearest for the session, pins the governor to .full via the re-inserted liveEditingDrops entry (1782), and on the next commit writes a session-scoped 'ROOM TEST' drop — an object explicitly documented as 'never persisted' (189-191, 1815) — to the user's on-disk library and up to Firestore. Repeated place/clear cycles also grow revealedDrops without bound, so a drop id that is re-placed never replays its ADR-046 reveal burst.
findings.fix: Replace the inline loop with `for id in roomDrops.keys { removePerDropState(id) }` before `roomDrops.removeAll()`. To make this class of omission structurally impossible, hoist all 16 per-drop collections into a single PerDropState value type with one `remove(_:)`, and add a Mirror-driven completeness test that fails when a new collection is added without a corresponding removal line.

findings.title: The SWE-5 vanish-guard is provably dead code; its nearestDrop fallback resurrects deleted drops into the library and the cloud
findings.trace: The Wave D comment at 1761-1763 claims 'a drop removed mid-drag clears the capture via removePerDropState' and the guard at 1766-1772 is written to bail and clear when the target vanished. It cannot execute. Proof: while editingDropID != nil, updateNearest returns at 1418 without writing nearestDrop, and the only other writers of nearestDrop are adjustNearestDrop itself (1779) and relocateNearestDrop (1977), both writing a value whose id equals the captured id. Therefore `nearestDrop?.id == id` is invariantly true whenever the capture is set, so the fourth arm at 1768 always yields a non-nil drop and the `else` block at 1769-1770 is unreachable. What the fallback does instead: after removePerDropState deletes a drop (1662/2155) it clears editingDropID (1407) but leaves nearestDrop stale until the next 400 ms tick recomputes it. An in-flight gesture's next slider tick re-captures that dead id (1764), resolves it through the fallback, writes placedDrops[id] = drop (1778), and on release calls library.update(edited, persist: true) (1826). DropStore.swift:917-923: `if let index = drops.firstIndex(...) { drops[index] = drop } else { drops.insert(drop, at: 0) }` — an absent id is INSERTED, then local.save(drop) and enqueueCloudSync(drop).
findings.harm: A drop the user (or its owner, or a walk out of the 2 km arVisibilityRadius) just removed comes back from the dead: re-inserted into the published library, re-written to disk, and re-uploaded to Firestore — directly contradicting remove()'s tombstone, pending-delete and cloud-delete bookkeeping (DropStore.swift:935-977), which has already run. The user deletes a drop and it reappears, and the cloud copy they believed destroyed is republished. The 400 ms race widens to unbounded whenever STATE-1 has frozen nearest, because then nearestDrop is stale indefinitely.
findings.fix: Resolve strictly from owned state — `placedDrops[id] ?? roomDrops[id] ?? demoDrops.first(where:)` — and bail on nil, restoring the guard to live code. Have removePerDropState clear nearestDrop/nearestDropDistance when the removed id is the current nearest, so the stale-nearest window closes at removal time rather than at the next tick. Extract the resolution as `nonisolated static func resolveEditTarget(id:placed:room:demo:)` so the bail is table-testable.

findings.title: Drop removal never invalidates the geospatial per-drop state: GARAnchors accumulate for the session and stale anchors silently re-own re-entering drops
findings.trace: removePerDropState (1395-1412) reaches 15 manager-side collections and zero engine-side ones. GeospatialEngine holds five per-drop maps — requestedDrops (62), resolvedDrops (63), garAnchorsByDropID (65), anchorIDToDropID (61), inFlightAnchorTokens (72) — and its per-drop invalidator (407-415) is called from exactly two places, both live-edit re-pins (1844, 1990). Neither removal loop calls it. requestAnchor (306) is issued for every eligible drop within AppConfig.arVisibilityRadius = 2000 m while VPS is accurately localized (1503-1507), so the sets grow monotonically with every drop ever passed. Second defect on the same axis: applyVPSTransform inserts into vpsOwnedDrops at 814, BEFORE the `guard let holder` bail at 815 — so every GAR update for a drop that no longer has a holder re-marks it VPS-owned.
findings.harm: (a) Unbounded live GARAnchors: each carries per-frame resolve cost inside geospatial.update (229-233) fed at up to 15 Hz (1242), and ARCore's resource-exhaustion state is mapped to `state = .failed("VPS: API quota exhausted")` (GeospatialEngine.swift:262) — one crossing kills the entire Tier C precision layer for the session, with isConverging then reporting false so the governor never sprints again. (b) Stale re-ownership: a drop that leaves the 2 km radius and returns is placed once from GPS, then permanently skipped by syncGPSPlacements because vpsOwnedDrops.contains(id) is true again (1590-1592), and is driven only by the anchor pinned at its PRE-EDIT coordinate. Because requestedDrops still contains the id (309), no re-pin is ever requested. If the creator moved the drop while the viewer was out of range, the viewer sees it permanently at the old location with no self-correction — a placement-truth failure that no other layer can heal.
findings.fix: Call `geospatial.invalidateAnchor(for: id)` from removePerDropState so engine-side per-drop state dies with the drop, and move `vpsOwnedDrops.insert(dropID)` (814) below the `guard let holder` bail (815) so a drop with no presence can never be marked owned. Give GeospatialEngine a protocol seam so the invalidation is assertable by a spy in the device suite.

findings.title: Wave D's scene-background listener teardown silently swallows every reaction that lands while the app is not in the foreground
findings.trace: scenePhase .background calls reactionService.stop() (203), which removes every registration AND clears primedListeners (ReactionService.swift:217-221). .active re-attaches (205 -> 114-167). The re-attached listener's first callback hits `guard self.primedListeners.contains(key) else { self.primedListeners.insert(key); return }` (153-156) and returns without toasting. The query is `.order(by: "at", descending: true).limit(to: 1)` (136), so that swallowed initial snapshot is exactly the newest reaction — i.e. the one that arrived while the app was backgrounded. Pre-Wave-D there was no scenePhase teardown: the listener survived, was already primed, and the SDK's reconnect delivered the row as a live `.added` change, so the toast fired on return. Confirmed there is no alternative sender-side surface: `incoming`/`incomingDropTitle` (RootView.swift:139-146) is the only one; `reactions(for:)` (191) is the VIEWER's Memory recap, reached only from MemoryScreen.swift:108. grep for Messaging / UNUserNotification / remoteNotification across the target returns nothing — no push channel exists, as the file's own header notes (lines 6-9).
findings.harm: The sender-side payoff of the product's core loop is lost in its single most common timing: share a link, pocket the phone, recipient reacts minutes later, sender returns — and is never told, in this session or any later one (the watermark is re-primed on every foreground, so the row is history forever). Wave D traded the loop's designed emotional payoff for battery and did not notice, because the item was framed as listener lifecycle rather than as delivery semantics. Wave C binding rule 6 applies directly: the test doubles for this seam do not reproduce the suspension mode that produces the bug.
findings.fix: Make the watermark durable rather than per-listener-instance: persist the last-seen reaction document id (or `at`) per drop key across stop(), and on re-attach toast any initial-snapshot `.added` row whose id is not the persisted one. Secondary: add a deinit to ReactionService that calls stop(), since FIRListenerRegistration does not detach on dealloc and a destroyed scene would otherwise leak live billed streams.

findings.title: A queued deep link is stranded when the receive sheet is dismissed without accepting — promotion is triggered only by a destination transition
findings.trace: onOpenURL queues into router.pendingReceiveDropID whenever `router.destination != nil || receiveDropID != nil` (100-107) — note the second disjunct fires even when destination is already nil. The sole promotion trigger is `.onChange(of: router.destination)` firing with destination == nil (109-114). Dismissing the `.sheet(item: $receiveDropID)` (115) mutates receiveDropID, not router.destination, so no onChange fires and the queued id sits in pendingReceiveDropID. It is only released the next time some unrelated cover happens to open and then close. The happy path masks it: accepting the invitation sets router.showCamera = true (134), and closing the camera later transitions destination to nil and promotes.
findings.harm: User has an invitation sheet up, taps a second magic link, dismisses the first without accepting — the second drop vanishes from the user's perspective. Later, opening and closing the camera or the create wizard for an unrelated reason pops an invitation for a link tapped minutes or hours earlier, with no context. SWE-7's claim is 'QUEUE ... and promote when the stage clears'; the stage-clear predicate only observes half the stage.
findings.fix: Define one computed `stageIsClear = router.destination == nil && receiveDropID == nil` and drive promotion from onChange of that predicate (or add a symmetric `.onChange(of: receiveDropID)`), so every way the stage clears releases the queue.

findings.title: Streetscape mesh backlog is unbounded, pins geometry buffers, and does the expensive work before the relevance check
findings.trace: syncOccluders enqueues one closure per NEW building geometry onto a single serial meshQueue (425, 445) with no cap, no priority ordering and no cancellation; the only gate is the per-id meshBuildsInFlight guard (441-442), which prevents duplicates but not volume. Each closure deliberately retains its GARStreetscapeGeometry to keep the vertex buffers valid (comment at 443), so a backlog of N pins N mesh buffers. The staleness guard `self.lastSeenGeometryIDs.contains(id)` (461) runs on the main-actor hop AFTER makeMeshDescriptor (446) and MeshResource.generate (451), so every building that streamed out during the backlog still costs a full scalar vertex/index extraction (497-512) plus a generate. Teardown is incomplete on the same axis: stop() (194-214) clears occluders and the root but not meshBuildsInFlight (426) or lastSeenGeometryIDs (429), and invalidateAllAnchors (392-402) — the explicit 'the world frame is new, every old-frame transform is garbage' reset — touches neither the occluders nor the in-flight builds. That teardown half is currently latent because detach()/geospatial.stop() has zero call sites app-wide.
findings.harm: Turning a corner onto a dense downtown block streams tens of building geometries in one GAR frame; the serial queue then runs at .userInitiated on a performance core for the entire backlog — including every building the user has already walked past — while holding tens of MB of GARMesh vertex buffers alive. ARP-7 correctly moved the stall off the main thread but left it unbounded, so on the exact dense urban block far-occlusion exists for, the cost reappears as sustained background CPU and memory pressure instead of a visible hitch. That is heat, against the same 10-minute thermal bar, produced by the fix for a frame-budget finding.
findings.fix: Re-check `lastSeenGeometryIDs.contains(id)` INSIDE the queue block before extraction so departed geometries cost nothing; cap the builds admitted per sync pass (e.g. 8, nearest-first by meshTransform distance) and let the rest be re-offered on a later frame; and clear meshBuildsInFlight + lastSeenGeometryIDs in stop(). Extract the admission decision as a pure `meshBuildPlan(present:inFlight:existing:budget:)` so the bound is table-testable.

findings.title: Tier B per-drop state has no removal path at all — geoAnchoredDropIDs and geoAnchors are append-only
findings.trace: tickGeoTracking only adds: `for drop in eligibleDrops where !geoAnchoredDropIDs.contains(drop.id)` creates an ARGeoAnchor and an AnchorEntity, appends to geoAnchors (2462) and inserts into geoAnchoredDropIDs (2463). There is no counterpart to the gpsCompass/transit removal loops, and removePerDropState (1395-1412) does not touch either collection. Only resetPlacements (769-770) clears them wholesale. renderedDropCount = geoAnchoredDropIDs.count (2465) is therefore monotonically non-decreasing in this mode. Gated off today by AppConfig.appleGeoAnchorsEnabled = false (AppConfig.swift:22), and the two modes are disjoint (a cold run always passes through resetPlacements), so nothing leaks across mode changes.
findings.harm: Latent. When the flag flips, a drop deleted by its owner or walked out of range keeps rendering as an ARGeoAnchor for the session, the anchor set grows without bound against ARKit's geo-anchor budget, and the HUD's 'N in view range' count only ever climbs. It is the last destroy-a-drop path Wave D did not unify, which is exactly the shape SWE-5 was filed against.
findings.fix: Give tickGeoTracking the same seen/remove discipline as tickGPSCompass: track the anchor entity per drop id, and on removal drop the ARGeoAnchor from the session, remove the AnchorEntity, and route the manager-side state through removePerDropState.

testCases.name: LiveEditRegistryTests.testAbandonedGestureExpiresAndReleasesTheGovernorPin
testCases.asserts: Proposed pure extraction: `struct LiveEditRegistry { mutating func begin(_ id: UUID, at: Date); mutating func tick(_ id: UUID, at: Date); mutating func commit(_ id: UUID); mutating func expire(now: Date) -> [UUID]; var capturedID: UUID?; var isLiveEditing: Bool }` with a 1.5 s abandon window, wired into GeoARSessionManager in place of editingDropID/liveEditingDrops. The test begins a gesture at t0, ticks at t0+0.2 (a drag in progress), delivers NO commit, then calls expire(now: t0+2.0) and asserts the returned abandoned set == [id], capturedID == nil, and isLiveEditing == false — i.e. updateNearest would unfreeze and PowerGovernor.Inputs.isLiveEditing would be false. A second case ticks at t0+0.2 and t0+1.0 then expires at t0+1.6 and asserts NOTHING is abandoned, proving the window measures inactivity rather than gesture age (no live drag is ever killed under the user's finger).
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: today's semantics have no expire path — the state is cleared only by commit, removePerDropState, or resetPlacements. A registry mirroring the shipped behaviour returns an empty abandoned set from expire and keeps capturedID set, so `XCTAssertEqual(abandoned, [id])`, `XCTAssertNil(capturedID)` and `XCTAssertFalse(isLiveEditing)` all fail. The test passes only once a time-based terminator exists.

testCases.name: SceneUnderstandingPolicyTests.testWindowModeExitRestoresOcclusionRegardlessOfLiveReconstructionState
testCases.asserts: Proposed pure extraction: `nonisolated static func wantsSceneOcclusion(occlusionCapable: Bool, pedestrian: Bool, windowModeActive: Bool) -> Bool`, used to re-derive sceneUnderstanding.options every tick after updatePowerTier. Table: (capable:true, pedestrian:true, window:true) -> false; (capable:true, pedestrian:true, window:false) -> true; (capable:true, pedestrian:false, window:false) -> false; (capable:false, ...) -> false. The load-bearing assertion is that the function's signature contains no reconstruction/appliedPerception term at all, so the exit decision cannot be poisoned by a transient perception state. Paired sequence test on the manager seam: drive windowModeActive true -> reconstruction false (camera hidden) -> windowModeActive false -> reconstruction true, and assert wantsSceneOcclusion is true at the end.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: the shipped decision at line 1032 is `if occlusionActive, renderPath == .pedestrian`, and occlusionActive == appliedPerception.reconstruction (1119). Replaying the sequence against today's code leaves .occlusion absent after the final step, so the terminal assertion fails. It also fails against pre-Wave-D code for a different reason worth pinning: there occlusionActive was a capability constant, so the third table row (transit) would wrongly return true — the test locks BOTH regressions out.

testCases.name: PerDropStateTests.testRemoveClearsEveryPerDropCollectionForTheID
testCases.asserts: Proposed extraction: hoist all 16 per-drop collections into `struct PerDropState` with a single `mutating func remove(_ id: UUID)`. The test populates EVERY stored property with an entry for a target id plus one entry for a bystander id, calls remove(target), then uses `Mirror(reflecting: state).children` to walk every stored property and assert that none of them still contains the target key/element, while every one still contains the bystander. A second case asserts `clearRoomDrops`-equivalent (`removeAll(where: isRoomDrop)`) leaves editingDropID nil and revealedDrops empty. Reflection is the point: a collection added in Wave E without a matching removal line fails this test automatically.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: written against today's shape, the clearRoomDrops case fails on two properties — editingDropID is still the cleared room drop's id and revealedDrops still contains it (populated by frameUpdate:2328 via the marker loop). The Mirror walk names the offending properties in the failure message, which is exactly the diagnostic the three-ad-hoc-loops history needed.

testCases.name: EditTargetResolutionTests.testResolveReturnsNilWhenTheCapturedDropIsGone
testCases.asserts: Proposed pure extraction: `nonisolated static func resolveEditTarget(id: UUID, placed: [UUID: GeoDrop], room: [UUID: GeoDrop], demo: [GeoDrop]) -> GeoDrop?`. Table: present in placed -> that drop; present only in room -> that drop; present only in demo -> that drop; present in NONE -> nil. A companion behavioural test drives the manager seam: capture a gesture on drop D, simulate D's removal (removePerDropState), deliver one more non-commit tick and then a commit, and assert (a) library.update was never called for D, (b) placedDrops has no entry for D, (c) editingDropID is nil, (d) liveEditingDrops is empty.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: today's expression carries a fourth arm, `?? (nearestDrop?.id == id ? nearestDrop : nil)` (1768), which is invariantly satisfied while the capture is set. A resolver mirroring the shipped expression returns the stale drop for the fourth table row, so `XCTAssertNil` fails; and the behavioural test fails assertions (a) and (b) because the commit reaches DropStore.update, which INSERTS the removed drop (DropStore.swift:921).

testCases.name: GeospatialLifecycleTests.testRemovingADropInvalidatesItsAnchorAndNeverReMarksItVPSOwned
testCases.asserts: Introduce a `GeospatialAnchoring` protocol seam (requestAnchor / invalidateAnchor / invalidateAllAnchors) and inject a spy. Part 1: place three drops, let the spy record one requestAnchor each, then shrink the eligible set to one drop so the removal loop runs; assert the spy recorded invalidateAnchor for exactly the two removed ids and none for the survivor. Part 2 (the ownership half): with drop D removed, deliver an onDropTransform callback for D (the shape a still-live GARAnchor produces) and assert D is NOT present in vpsOwnedDrops afterwards; then re-add D to the eligible set and assert syncGPSPlacements actually positions it from GPS on the following tick rather than skipping it at line 1590.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: today removePerDropState never calls invalidateAnchor, so the spy records zero calls and Part 1 fails on the first assertion. Part 2 fails because applyVPSTransform inserts into vpsOwnedDrops at 814 before the holder guard at 815, so the removed id is re-marked owned and the re-added drop is skipped by the `vpsOwnedDrops.contains` branch.

testCases.name: ReactionDeliveryTests.testReactionArrivingWhileBackgroundedIsToastedOnReturn
testCases.asserts: Per Wave C binding rule 6, the double must reproduce production's SUSPENSION mode, not just its success mode: a FakeReactionBackend that (a) emits an initial snapshot on every attach containing the newest row, (b) emits subsequent rows as `.added` changes, and (c) models stop() as a hard detach that drops all in-flight delivery. Sequence: attach for drop D; emit reaction R0 in the initial snapshot; assert incoming == nil (history, correct). Emit R1 live; assert incoming?.id == R1. Call stop(). Emit R2 into the backend while detached. Re-attach. Assert incoming?.id == R2 and incomingDropTitle == D.title. A second case asserts that a re-attach with NO new row since the last teardown produces incoming == nil, so the fix cannot be a blanket 'toast the initial snapshot'.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: stop() clears primedListeners (ReactionService.swift:220), so on re-attach the guard at 153-156 classifies R2's snapshot as priming and returns — incoming stays nil and the first assertion of the third step fails. The second case passes today (vacuously) and is what stops the naive fix, so both are required.

testCases.name: DeepLinkQueueTests.testQueuedLinkPromotesWhenTheReceiveSheetIsDismissed
testCases.asserts: Proposed extraction of the presentation stage as a small observable model: `struct ReceiveStage { var destination: AppRouter.Destination?; var presentedDropID: UUID?; var queued: UUID?; var isClear: Bool { destination == nil && presentedDropID == nil }; mutating func offer(_ id: UUID); mutating func stageDidChange() }`. Cases: (1) offer while presentedDropID != nil and destination == nil -> queued == id, presented unchanged; then set presentedDropID = nil and call stageDidChange -> presented == id, queued == nil. (2) offer while destination == .camera -> queued; destination = nil, stageDidChange -> promoted. (3) offer on a clear stage -> presented immediately, queued == nil.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: today's promotion lives only in `.onChange(of: router.destination)` (RootView.swift:109-114), so case (1) — where destination never changes value — leaves pendingReceiveDropID set and receiveDropID nil. A model mirroring the shipped triggers fails case (1)'s promotion assertion while cases (2) and (3) pass, isolating exactly the stranded path.

testCases.name: StreetscapeMeshPlanTests.testBuildPlanIsBoundedAndExcludesDepartedGeometries
testCases.asserts: Proposed pure extraction: `nonisolated static func meshBuildPlan(present: [(id: UUID, distance: Float)], inFlight: Set<UUID>, existing: Set<UUID>, budget: Int) -> [UUID]`. Cases: (1) 40 present, none in flight or existing, budget 8 -> exactly 8 ids returned, and they are the 8 nearest (bounded + prioritised). (2) an id in `existing` or `inFlight` is never returned. (3) admission is idempotent across two calls with the same inputs (no duplicate enqueue). Companion unit on the worker: `shouldBuild(id:lastSeen:)` must be consulted BEFORE makeMeshDescriptor — asserted by a descriptor factory spy that must record zero invocations for an id absent from lastSeen. Plus a teardown case: after stop(), meshBuildsInFlight and lastSeenGeometryIDs are both empty.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: today syncOccluders (431-470) has no budget parameter and no ordering, so a planner mirroring it returns all 40 ids and case (1) fails on count. The descriptor-factory spy records 1 invocation for the departed id because the staleness check sits at line 461, after generate — so that assertion fails too. The teardown case fails because stop() (194-214) clears neither collection.

testCases.name: GeoTrackingAnchorLifecycleTests.testAnchorsAreRemovedWhenTheirDropLeavesTheEligibleSet
testCases.asserts: With AppConfig.appleGeoAnchorsEnabled forced true via an injected config, run tickGeoTracking with drops {A, B, C}; assert geoAnchoredDropIDs == {A, B, C} and renderedDropCount == 3. Shrink the eligible set to {A}; run the tick again; assert geoAnchoredDropIDs == {A}, renderedDropCount == 1, the session recorded remove(anchor:) for B and C, and geoAnchors.count == 1 (the array is not append-only). A fourth assertion adds B back and requires exactly one new anchor, proving removal did not leave a re-add gate stuck.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: tickGeoTracking (2426-2466) contains no removal branch at all — geoAnchoredDropIDs stays {A, B, C}, renderedDropCount stays 3, zero remove(anchor:) calls are recorded, and geoAnchors.count stays 3. All four assertions of the second phase fail. The test is written now and gated off with the flag so the path cannot ship unguarded when the flag flips.

cleanAreas: removePerDropState itself is complete for the manager side: verified line-by-line against the full inventory of per-drop collections (grep of every `[UUID:` / `Set<UUID>` declaration, lines 122-301) — all 15 reachable collections plus editingDropID are cleared (1396-1411), and both removal loops (1662, 2155) route through it. Mutating placedHolders inside `for (id, _) in placedHolders` is safe: Swift iterates a COW copy.

resetPlacements (760-804) is complete for every manager-side per-drop collection, including the two Wave D additions (revealedDrops at 785, editingDropID at 782) and the Tier B sets (769-770). No gap found.

applyPerceptionHysteresis (1195-1215) is correct as specified: upgrades are immediate, downgrades require 10 s of continuous absence AND `applied == true`, and the `guard applied` arm (1202-1205) means a stream that is already off can never be re-raised by the hysteresis itself. personDownSince/depthDownSince self-heal after runGPSCompass resets appliedPerception (714), so no reset gap exists there.

perceptionPlan (1161-1189) is total over cameraVisible — every term is conjoined with it — and each depth clause carries its own precondition (supportsCustomPersonOcclusion for the person leg, midFieldEnabled && pedestrian && fullTier for the mid-field leg), so the request genuinely derives from the same predicate as the use. The seven table tests cover the transit, thermal, presence-cycle and camera-hidden axes correctly.

The ARScreen syncSliders / frozen-nearest interplay is correct during a NORMAL drag: adjustNearestDrop rewrites nearestDrop with the same id (1779), so `.onChange(of: manager.nearestDrop?.id)` (ARScreen.swift:573) does not fire and the slider is never yanked out from under the user's finger mid-gesture. This was the specific mechanism SWE-5 named, and it is genuinely fixed.

AppRouter's transitions are each one state change and the compat accessors are consistent with the enum: showCamera=false during the demo returns to .onboardingStory in a single write (AppRouter.swift:54-56), finishOnboarding only clears its own destination (104), and destinationBinding centralises the four dismissal side effects (RootView.swift:27-38) without any of them being duplicated at a direct-write site. The five router tests cover the transitions that matter.

GeospatialEngine's anchor-token discipline is sound: every request stamps a token (310-312), both completion paths compare it before registering and remove the orphaned anchor when superseded (337-340, 362-365), and invalidateAllAnchors/invalidateAnchor clear the token so an in-flight completion becomes stale (400, 410). No resurrection path found on that axis.

The streetscape build pipeline is correctly ISOLATED even though it is unbounded: meshBuildsInFlight, occluders, lastSeenGeometryIDs and occluderCount are mutated only on the main actor (441-442, 453-467, 471-476), the background block touches only the nonisolated static extractor and the retained geometry, and the per-id in-flight gate prevents duplicate enqueues. There is no data race here — only a volume/teardown problem (STATE-8).

The gesture-identity half is CLOSED: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1764 captures `editingDropID` at gesture start, :1766-1771 bails and clears when the target vanished, :1418 freezes `updateNearest()` while a drag is live, :1834-1835 clears on commit, :1395-1412 `removePerDropState` is the single cleanup helper used by both removal loops (:1662, :2155) and clears `editingDropID`, :781-782 resetPlacements clears it too. The half that fails is TEARDOWN: the freeze is released only by `commit: true` (ARScreen.swift:488-491 `onEditingChanged(false)`) or a full `resetPlacements()`. `markCameraHidden()` (:466-468) and `suspendSession()` (:402-415) leave `editingDropID`/`liveEditingDrops` set, so a cover swapped out from under a live drag pins the governor to `.full` forever (:1064) and freezes nearest-drop tracking. See FLOW-5.

The single cover exists (App/RootView.swift:60 `fullScreenCover(item: destinationBinding)`, App/AppRouter.swift:28-34 `Destination`) and memory→create is genuinely one change (RootView.swift:81-86, MemoryScreen.swift:95-100). But: (1) a SECOND presentation modifier still sits on the same view — RootView.swift:115 `.sheet(item: $receiveDropID)`; (2) the receive hand-off is still a dismiss+present pair — ReceiveScreen.swift:117-120 calls `onReveal` (RootView.swift:134 `router.showCamera = true`) then `dismiss()` in the same closure (FLOW-2); (3) the deep-link queue promotes into a dismissing presenter and has no promotion trigger when the blocker was the receive sheet (RootView.swift:100-114, FLOW-3); (4) collapsing the stacked covers destroyed OnboardingView's `beat` @State, making onboarding beat 3 unreachable (OnboardingView.swift:14,151 + AppRouter.swift:90-99, FLOW-1); (5) the 'dismissal side effects centralized in destinationBinding' claim only holds for `.create` and `.memory` — nothing calls `dismiss()` for `.camera` or `.onboardingStory`, and programmatic `router.destination = …` never invokes the setter, so RootView.swift:30-38 is dead for those two cases (contributes to FLOW-4). Router state tests (WaveDTests.swift:139-190) assert scalars only and cannot fail on any of this.

The teardown half is CLOSED: RootView.swift:200-209 `.background` → `reactionService.stop()` (ReactionService.swift:217-221 removes listeners and clears `primedListeners`), `.active` → re-attach, and Wave C's primed watermark (ReactionService.swift:150-161) makes the re-attach snapshot history. No deinit is defensible: `reactionService` is a root `@StateObject` (RootView.swift:14) alive for the process. The user-visible half is not closed: the toast the listener exists to deliver is rendered UNDER every cover and self-clears after 4 s (RootView.swift:138-163), so reactions arriving while the sender is in AR/create/memory are consumed invisibly and permanently (FLOW-9).

findings.title: Onboarding beat 3 is unreachable: the SWE-7 single-cover model destroys OnboardingView's @State on the fireworks hand-off
findings.trace: `beat` is `@State private var beat = 0` (OnboardingView.swift:14). `startDemo()` sets `beat = 2` with the comment 'beat 3 waits underneath for the return' (OnboardingView.swift:151) and then calls `router.beginFireworksDemo()` (:153 → AppRouter.swift:90-93: `destination = .camera`). Under the OLD stacked-cover shape the story cover really did stay presented underneath. Under Wave D there is exactly ONE cover (RootView.swift:60) whose content is a `switch destination` (RootView.swift:61-90): setting `destination = .camera` tears OnboardingView out of the hierarchy, discarding `beat`. `endFireworksDemo()` (AppRouter.swift:96-99) sets `destination = .onboardingStory`, which constructs a FRESH OnboardingView at `beat = 0`. Nothing restores it — OnboardingView never reads `router.onboardingPhase`, and the only other beat mutation is :63 (`beat = 1`).
findings.harm: First run, 100% reproducible, no device state required: promise → 'Show me' → 'Light fireworks on my floor' → live camera → 'Magical — continue' → the user lands back on beat 0 ('Hide magic in the real world'). The name beat is unreachable via the designed path, so `displayName` is never captured and `account.updateProfile` (OnboardingView.swift:116) never runs — every drop the user creates is authored under the default name. A user who keeps tapping the obvious CTA loops promise→demo→promise forever, and each cycle re-runs `beginRevealWarmup()` + a fresh `placeRoomDrop(.fireworks)` (OnboardingView.swift:152-162) — repeated camera bring-up and fireworks placement, i.e. a heat path with no exit. The only escape is 'Skip' (:30), which sets `hasOnboarded = true` with no name. This is a review-blocking first-run defect introduced BY the Wave D fix.
findings.fix: Move the beat out of the view: add `@Published var onboardingBeat: Int = 0` to AppRouter, have `beginFireworksDemo()` set it to 2 and `endFireworksDemo()` leave it at 2, and bind OnboardingView to `router.onboardingBeat` instead of local @State. Add an assertion in the router test that a story→camera→story round trip preserves the beat.

findings.title: Receive→camera is still a dismiss()+present pair across two presentation modifiers on one view — the acquisition path SWE-7 did not fix
findings.trace: RootView still carries TWO presentation modifiers on the same view: `.fullScreenCover(item: destinationBinding)` at :60 and `.sheet(item: $receiveDropID)` at :115 — the exact 'three covers plus a .sheet on one view' shape the SWE-7 comment (AppRouter.swift:20-27) declares unsupported, only reduced from four channels to two. In ReceiveScreen.swift:117-120 the CTA closure runs `onReveal(drop)` and then `dismiss()`. `onReveal` is RootView.swift:116-135, whose last statement is `router.showCamera = true` → AppRouter.swift:46-51 → `destination = .camera`. So one synchronous transaction both requests a fullScreenCover and dismisses the sheet that is currently presented from the same presenter.
findings.harm: Tap magic link → 'Reveal in AR' → the sheet closes and the camera cover is dropped (UIKit refuses a present on a controller whose `presentedViewController` is mid-dismissal). The user is returned to Home with `reactionSession.drop` set and `phase == .watching` (ReactionSession.swift:29-37) but no AR surface — `ReactionOverlay` exists only inside ARScreen (ARScreen.swift:26-30), so there is zero UI acknowledging the received drop, no reaction bar, no wrap, no Memory. The redeem Task (RootView.swift:124-132) has already persisted the drop, so the invitation cannot be replayed except by re-tapping the link. This is the product's entire acquisition loop failing silently on a timing-dependent presenter state — exactly the class Wave D was chartered on.
findings.fix: Fold receive into the single destination: `case receive(UUID)` on `AppRouter.Destination`, so link → invitation → camera are three values of one enum and each transition is one state change. If the sheet must stay, move the hand-off into `.sheet(item:onDismiss:)` so `router.destination = .camera` runs only after the sheet has finished dismissing.

findings.title: Queued deep link promotes into a dismissing presenter, and has no promotion trigger at all when the blocker was the receive sheet
findings.trace: `.onOpenURL` (RootView.swift:100-108) queues into `router.pendingReceiveDropID` when `router.destination != nil` OR `receiveDropID != nil`. The ONLY promotion is `.onChange(of: router.destination)` (:109-114), which fires the instant `destination` becomes nil — i.e. at the START of the cover's dismissal, not at its end — and immediately assigns `receiveDropID`, so the sheet at :115 is requested while the cover is still on screen (same defect shape as FLOW-2). Second, independent hole: if the link arrived while `destination == nil` and `receiveDropID != nil` (the :102 guard's second clause), the queue is keyed to a `destination` transition that never happens; closing the receive sheet changes `receiveDropID`, which has no `onChange`. Third: `pendingReceiveDropID` is a single slot (:105) — a second queued link overwrites the first with no record.
findings.harm: (a) User is watching drop A in the camera, taps a link for drop B, closes the camera → B's invitation is requested into a dismissing presenter and can vanish; the user sees the camera close and nothing else, with no way to recover B except re-tapping the link. (b) User has A's invitation open, taps a link for B → B is queued and then stranded indefinitely: dismissing A's sheet promotes nothing, and B only surfaces if some unrelated cover happens to open and close later — at which point an invitation for a drop the user tapped minutes ago ambushes them out of context. Both are the 'deep link tapped while a cover is up is silently lost' bug the item claims to have closed.
findings.fix: Put the state machine on AppRouter as pure methods — `func linkArrived(_ id: UUID, coverUp: Bool, receiveUp: Bool)` and `func promotePendingReceive(coverUp: Bool, receiveUp: Bool) -> UUID?` — and call `promotePendingReceive` from BOTH `onChange(of: router.destination)` and `onChange(of: receiveDropID)`, performing the actual present from `fullScreenCover(item:onDismiss:content:)`'s `onDismiss` so it never lands mid-dismissal. Table-test the machine.

findings.title: Closing the camera does not end the watch session: a Memory cover ambushes the user later and can destroy an in-progress Create draft
findings.trace: `.onChange(of: reactionSession.phase) { if phase == .memory { router.destination = .memory } }` (RootView.swift:94-96) is unconditional — it does not check that the camera is the current destination. Leaving the camera does not touch the session: ARScreen.swift:151-156 calls `router.showCamera = false` → AppRouter.swift:46-57 sets `destination = nil` directly, which never invokes `destinationBinding.set` (RootView.swift:20-42), and even if it did, the `.camera` case (:35-38) only handles the fireworks demo. `ReactionSession.wrapTask` keeps ticking (ReactionSession.swift:89-102) and fires `phase = .memory` 15 s after the first reaction regardless of what is on screen.
findings.harm: Watch a received drop → tap ❤️ (starts the 15 s wrap, ReactionSession.swift:59-62) → tap the ADR-048 escape chevron at t+3 s → 12 s later a full-screen Memory cover appears over whatever the user is now doing. If they had tapped the create orb (RootView.swift:245), the Memory cover REPLACES the live CreateWizard and destroys every @State in it — chosen surprise, pinned coordinate, recipient name, message (CreateWizard.swift:26-52) — with no warning and no way back; the user's half-composed gift is gone. The Memory itself is also degraded: the snapshot is captured by ARScreen's own `onChange` (ARScreen.swift:31-37), which cannot fire once ARScreen is gone, so `snapshot == nil` and MemoryScreen falls back to the text card (MemoryScreen.swift:129-133) — the loop's payoff artifact, and the only thing 'Save memory' can write to Photos (:220-224), is empty.
findings.fix: Gate the presentation on context: `if phase == .memory, router.destination == .camera { router.destination = .memory }`, and make leaving the camera end the ritual — route the escape button through a router method that calls `reactionSession.endSession()` when `reactionSession.drop != nil` (or park the wrap and resume it if the user returns). Also make the `.camera` and `.onboardingStory` dismissal side effects reachable by routing programmatic dismissals through the same helper the binding uses.

findings.title: A live slider drag torn down with the cover leaks editingDropID/liveEditingDrops: nearest tracking freezes for the session and the governor pins to .full
findings.trace: The freeze is released only by a commit: `updateNearest()` returns early while `editingDropID != nil` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1414-1418); `editingDropID`/`liveEditingDrops` are cleared at :1834-1835 only under `if commit`, and the only commit call sites are the sliders' `onEditingChanged(false)` handlers (ARScreen.swift:488-491, :509-512, :530-533). Nothing on the teardown path clears them: `cameraDidDisappear()` → `markCameraHidden()` sets only `cameraVisible = false` (:466-468); `suspendSession()` (:402-415) does not touch them; `removePerDropState` (:1395-1412) only runs when a specific drop is destroyed; `resetPlacements()` (:781-782) clears them but runs only on a cold `runGPSCompass()`. Two triggers remove ARScreen mid-drag with no editing-ended callback: (a) the wrap timer firing `phase == .memory` (RootView.swift:95) while the adjust panel is under the finger — the panel is NOT hidden while watching (ARScreen.swift:284-288 hides it only for `demoing`); (b) backgrounding mid-drag (AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:36-39 → ARSessionHolder.appDidEnterBackground → suspend).
findings.harm: Exactly the failure the code's own comment describes (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1391-1394): the leaked `liveEditingDrops` entry feeds `isLiveEditing: !liveEditingDrops.isEmpty` into the governor (:1064), pinning the power tier to `.full` — every perception stream at maximum for the rest of the process — which breaks the BRIEF bar 'NOT thermal .serious at 10 min'. Simultaneously `updateNearest()` never runs again, so the HUD's nearest-drop card, guidance arrow/bearing (ARScreen.swift:290-295) and the adjust panel's target stay pinned to a drop the user has walked away from, and 'Place on ground'/'Pin to a spot' act on that stale drop. The session cannot recover without a cold AR restart. Wave D closed the drop-removed-mid-drag leak and left the view-removed-mid-drag leak open.
findings.fix: Add `func cancelLiveEdit()` that commits-or-clears (`liveEditingDrops.removeAll(); editingDropID = nil`) and call it from `markCameraHidden()` and `suspendSession()`; assert in a device test that `powerTier` can return below `.full` after a camera-hidden cycle that began mid-drag.

findings.title: The camera cover has no escape affordance in two of its three render branches — an inescapable full-screen trap
findings.trace: The ADR-048 dismiss chevron is inside the `else if isActive, let arView = holder.arView` branch only (ARScreen.swift:148-170). The other two ZStack branches render without it: :101-106 (`!GeoARSessionManager.isDeviceSupported` → ContentUnavailableView) and :201-203 (`Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()` when `holder.arView == nil`). `fullScreenCover` is not interactively dismissible, and RootView passes `ARScreen(isActive: true)` unconditionally (RootView.swift:63), so there is no other exit. Reachability of `arView == nil` while presented: `startIfNeeded()` bails on `guard let locationService, let library else { return }` (ARSessionHolder.swift:94-96) and nothing retries; `configure(...)` runs from the App's async `.task` (AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:28-35) while `warmWithoutCamera()` runs only from `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` (:44), which does not fire for the initial `.active` value at launch. A cold launch straight into a magic link therefore has a real window in which `beginRevealWarmup()` (ReceiveScreen.swift:50) and then `cameraDidAppear()` both return without creating the ARView.
findings.harm: The user taps 'Reveal in AR' on a cold-launched link and gets a black full-screen cover with no HUD, no content and no way out — force-quit is the only recovery, and the received drop is consumed. Same trap on any device where `ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.isSupported` is false: the 'AR needs a real iPhone' card is presented full-screen with no close button. This is a hard-stop UX trap on the acquisition path and reads as a hang in a review.
findings.fix: Move the dismiss button out of the branch — attach it as an `.overlay(alignment: .topLeading)` on the ZStack so it renders in every state — and make it visually above `revealOverlay` (currently :197-200 paints an opaque `Night.bgScreen` over it for up to `revealMaxSeconds`). Separately, have `ARScreenContent.onAppear` retry `holder.cameraDidAppear()` (or observe `holder.arView`) so a lost configure race self-heals.

findings.title: The ARP-6 UNCAPPED format evidence is invisible in exactly the sessions that need it
findings.trace: `videoFormatDescription` — the string carrying `· UNCAPPED` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:672-679) — is rendered only as the tail of `metricsLine(ttfo:)` (ARScreen.swift:623-629), and that line is gated on `if let ttfo = manager.timeToFirstObjectMs` (:446). `timeToFirstObjectMs` is nil unless content is actually placed: `markCameraVisible()` sets 0 only when `!placedHolders.isEmpty`, else nil (GeoARSessionManager.swift:474-480), and `recordTTFOIfNeeded()` requires `!placedHolders.isEmpty` (:2024-2028). The whole HUD is additionally removed by a stray tap (`hudHidden`, ARScreen.swift:110-118).
findings.harm: On a device where the format policy is unsatisfiable, the session runs ARKit's platform default (potentially 4K@60 — the exact ADR-034 heat bug) and the HUD says nothing at all whenever the user opens the camera somewhere with no drops: the first-run Playground, an empty neighbourhood, or a field test that never localizes. The counsel's stated field-evidence surface for the highest-leverage heat control is conditioned on an unrelated killer-#1 metric, so the one class of device that most needs the marker is the least likely to show it.
findings.fix: Render the format as its own chip in `statusCard` alongside LiDAR/SEM/DPT (ARScreen.swift:360-400), tinted red when the description contains `UNCAPPED`, independent of `timeToFirstObjectMs`; keep the metrics line as-is.

findings.title: occlusionActive conflates request with capability — the blue 'LiDAR' chip lights on every non-LiDAR device
findings.trace: `perceptionPlan` computes `let reconstruction = cameraVisible && pedestrian && !thermalCritical` with no capability term (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1178). `setPerception` stores it unconditionally: `appliedPerception = desired` (:751), even though `makeConfiguration` drops the stream unless supported — `if reconstruction, ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsSceneReconstruction(.mesh)` (:622). Then `occlusionActive = appliedPerception.reconstruction` (:1119) and ARScreen.swift:372-374 renders `chip("LiDAR", color: .blue)`. Wave D's own item-5 note claims the pedestrian branch 're-inserts .occlusion from device capability', but `setWindowMode(false)` keys on `occlusionActive` (:1032), not on the `occlusionCapable` predicate computed at attach (:715-717).
findings.harm: On an iPhone 14/15 base, SE, or any non-LiDAR handset — most of the install base — the HUD asserts LiDAR occlusion is active whenever the camera is up in pedestrian mode, while `config.sceneReconstruction` was never set and no depth occlusion is running. The counsel and field testers judge the BRIEF bar 'zero draw-over-known-front-surface frames' against this chip; it now reports a stream that is not configured, so a genuine occlusion failure on that hardware reads as 'LiDAR was on, must be a shader bug'. It also makes `appliedPerception` an unreliable record of the session's real configuration for every downstream consumer.
findings.fix: Gate at the source: add `supportsSceneReconstruction: Bool` to `perceptionPlan` and AND it into the reconstruction term, so `appliedPerception` can never claim an unapplied stream; belt-and-braces, set `occlusionActive = appliedPerception.reconstruction && ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsSceneReconstruction(.mesh)` at :1119 and key :1032 on capability.

findings.title: Incoming-reaction toasts and the global persist-error banner are rendered UNDER every cover and self-clear while invisible
findings.trace: The toast is `.overlay(alignment: .top)` on the ZStack that holds `screen` + `NightTabBar` (RootView.swift:44-49, :138-163) — a sibling of the tab content, therefore beneath every `fullScreenCover` presented at :60. Its `.task` still runs while covered and calls `reactionService.clearIncoming()` after 4 s (:158-161 → ReactionService.swift:213-214), and there is no unread store. The persist-error banner at :169-186 — added in round 4 as the 'global backstop' because failures fired from the Map or the receive flow were invisible — has the same placement and is likewise covered by camera/create/memory.
findings.harm: A sender who is in the camera, composing a create, or on the Memory screen when a friend reacts never sees the toast, and it is destroyed 4 s later — the reciprocity beat that the whole listener lifecycle (SWE-10/PBS-9) exists to deliver is dropped precisely when the user is most engaged with the app. Same for save failures raised while a cover is up: the 'global' banner is not global, so a persist failure during the create ritual or the receive redeem can be shown to nobody (only ARScreen's own `persistErrorText`, :407-412, survives, and only in the camera).
findings.fix: Hoist both overlays above the presentation — attach them inside each destination's content as well, or present them from a separate window-level overlay — and suppress the 4 s auto-clear while `router.destination != nil` so the toast is delivered when the stage clears.

findings.title: Home's 'WAITING FOR YOU' card opens the camera without starting the watch session — the react→memory loop is link-only
findings.trace: `forYouCard(_:)` builds a Button over a specific received `drop` but its action is only `router.showCamera = true` (HomeScreen.swift:145-147); it never calls `reactionSession.startWatching(drop)`. The link path does both (RootView.swift:133-134). `ReactionOverlay` is gated on `reactionSession.drop != nil` (ARScreen.swift:27-29), and `phase` stays `.idle`, so no reaction bar, no wrap, no Memory. The Playground card (:213) and the Map viewfinder button (MapScreen.swift:84) share the shape, which is correct for those two.
findings.harm: Anyone who dismisses the invitation and comes back later via the obvious 'you're here — open the camera →' card (HomeScreen.swift:174-180) gets a plain viewfinder: they can see the drop but cannot react, the sender is never told it was opened, and no Memory is produced. The product's core loop — PRODUCT-ROUTE §0 receive→watch→react→memory — is reachable only from a freshly tapped magic link.

findings.title: No test exercises a presentation: the SWE-7 suite asserts router scalars and cannot fail when a cover is dropped
findings.trace: `AppRouterDestinationTests` (WaveDTests.swift:139-190) constructs a bare `AppRouter` and asserts `destination`/`onboardingPhase` after direct calls. Every mechanism SWE-7 was chartered to protect lives in RootView and is untested: the two-modifier interleaving (:60 vs :115), the queue/promote machine (:100-114), the phase→memory rule (:94-96), and the identity swaps on a LIVE cover (onboardingStory→camera, camera→onboardingStory, camera→memory, memory→create). Wave C binding rule 6 requires doubles to reproduce production's isolation, suspension and failure modes; the double here is an enum assignment, which has no presenter, cannot suspend mid-dismissal and cannot drop. Each of FLOW-1 … FLOW-4 passes this suite unchanged.
findings.harm: The wave's own evidence (18 new tests, 130/130 green) reads as coverage of the presentation fix while covering none of it, which is how FLOW-1 (a 100%-reproducible first-run break) shipped as 'CLOSED'. Any future refactor of RootView has no regression net at all.
findings.fix: Extract the presentation policy into pure, table-testable router methods — `linkArrived(_:coverUp:receiveUp:)`, `promotePendingReceive(coverUp:receiveUp:)`, `memoryBecameReady(cameraUp:)`, `cameraDismissed(watching:)`, `onboardingBeat` — and test them as state machines; add one XCUITest that walks onboarding → fireworks → back → name → finish and one that opens a link while the camera cover is up and asserts the invitation actually appears.

testCases.name: testOnboardingReturnsToTheNameBeatAfterTheFireworksDemo

The XCUITest half compiles and runs against the current build and fails on the assertion: the returned cover is a fresh OnboardingView at beat 0, so 'Hide magic in the real world' is on screen and 'Who's dropping?' never appears. testCases.name: testRevealHandoffIsOneDestinationChangeNotADismissPresentPair

testCases.name: testQueuedLinkPromotesWhenTheReceiveSheetClosesAndNeverMidDismissal
testCases.asserts: Table-test `promotePendingReceive(coverUp:receiveUp:)`: (a) queue while a cover is up → promote returns the id when called with `coverUp:false, receiveUp:false`; (b) queue while the receive sheet is up with NO cover → closing the sheet (`receiveUp:false`) promotes the id; (c) two links queued → assert the router records both (FIFO) and promotes them in order; (d) assert `promotePendingReceive` returns nil while `coverUp` is true. testCases.failsWhen: Case (b) is the vacuity proof: today the only promotion trigger is `onChange(of: router.destination)` (RootView.swift:109), so a queue whose blocker was `receiveDropID` has no trigger — the id stays in `pendingReceiveDropID` forever and the assertion fails. Case (c) fails because `pendingReceiveDropID` is a single overwritten slot (:105). The XCUITest fails with B never appearing. All pass once promotion is a router method driven by both blockers.

testCases.name: testMemoryNeverPresentsAfterTheCameraIsDismissed

testCases.name: testRootPresentationStateMachineIsTableTestable
testCases.asserts: A single suite over the extracted router methods covering the full transition table: story→camera→story preserves the beat; link-while-cover queues and promotes exactly once; link-while-receive-sheet promotes on sheet close; memory presents only when the camera is up; camera dismissal ends a live watch; create is never replaced by memory. Plus two XCUITests (onboarding walk-through, deep-link-while-camera-open) that assert real presentations, not state.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity proof: none of these methods exist today — the logic is inline in RootView's modifier closures (RootView.swift:94-114, :20-42), which no XCTest can reach — so the suite cannot be written against the current build at all; that impossibility is the finding. Once extracted, each row fails against the current behaviour (FLOW-1 … FLOW-4) and passes only after those fixes, while the existing `AppRouterDestinationTests` (WaveDTests.swift:139-190) stays green throughout, demonstrating that the shipped suite has no power over this class of defect.

cleanAreas: Create-from-map prefill cleanup is correct end to end: MapScreen.swift:47 and :98 call `router.beginCreate(at:)` (AppRouter.swift:74-77), CreateWizard exits via `dismiss()` (CreateWizard.swift:93 from the share sheet's onDismiss, and :116 from the close control), which routes through `destinationBinding.set(nil)` → RootView.swift:28-29 `router.createPrefill = nil`. `beginCreate()` also reassigns `createPrefill` on every entry, so even a programmatic destination swap that skips the binding cannot leak a stale pin into the next ritual.

MemoryScreen's 'Send one back' is genuinely one destination change: MemoryScreen.swift:95-100 calls the injected closure, which is RootView.swift:81-86 `reactionSession.endSession(); router.beginCreate()` — no `dismiss()`, no racing binding. The intermediate state (drop nil, destination still .memory) is inside one synchronous transaction, so the `if let drop` guard at RootView.swift:74 can never render an empty cover.

The onboarding/demo compat setter is symmetric and correct as state: `showCamera = false` during `.fireworksDemo` returns to `.onboardingStory` and demotes the phase in one assignment (AppRouter.swift:52-56), matching both explicit call sites (ARScreen.swift:152-153 and :181) and the binding's `.camera` case (RootView.swift:35-38). Covered by WaveDTests.swift:151-166.

The capture-format policy is a genuinely pure, well-bounded function: GeoARSessionManager.swift:687-705 enforces fps ≤ target AND area ∈ [1280×720 … 1920×1440] with highest-fps-then-smallest-area preference, and the unsatisfiable branch is loud in both the log and the HUD string (:672-679). The only defect is where that string is rendered (FLOW-7), not the policy.

The perception hysteresis is correct and non-oscillating: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1194-1213 upgrades immediately, starts the 10 s downgrade clock only when the stream is actually applied, and never re-raises a stream that is already off — so a person stepping out of frame cannot cycle `session.run` on the 400 ms tick.

ReactionSession's send-token identity is sound for every flow I drove: `startWatching` bumps the token (ReactionSession.swift:33) and each of `reactionDelivered`/`reactionQueued`/`reactionFailed` guards on it (:66-81), so a late completion for a previous drop cannot repaint the Memory screen's delivery badge (MemoryScreen.swift:181-197). The wrap task's cancel/phase guards (:92-102) are race-free under MainActor isolation.

ShareDropSheet nesting is legitimate: CreateWizard.swift:91-95 presents it from inside the create cover (a different presenter) and chains `onDismiss: { dismiss() }`, so the wizard exits sequentially rather than as a same-update dismiss+present pair.

ownFindings.title: The FLOW-1 onboarding loop accumulates one fireworks room drop per cycle — an unbounded particle/entity leak with no user-reachable clear
ownFindings.trace: placeRoomDrop (GeoARSessionManager.swift:510-551) mints a NEW GeoDrop with a fresh UUID on every call, inserts it into roomDrops/placedDrops/placedHolders and calls DropEntityFactory.startAnimations(on:) — it never clears prior room drops. OnboardingView.startDemo (OnboardingView.swift:150-163) calls arHolder.beginRevealWarmup() then, after the frame-ready poll, manager.placeRoomDrop(content: .fireworks) EVERY time it runs. Because FLOW-1 returns the user to beat 0 (the @State is destroyed by the single-cover swap), the only forward CTA is 'Show me' → 'Light fireworks on my floor' → startDemo again. The one clear path, clearRoomDrops (554-568), is reachable only from the HUD room-test controls, and hudOverlay hides that whole block while `demoing` (ARScreen.swift:284-288 gates adjustPanel/room controls on `!demoing`). So nothing in the onboarding loop ever clears them.
ownFindings.harm: Device: first run, user follows the designed CTA. Each loop iteration adds a persistent fireworks emitter entity under worldRoot (they are all within a couple of metres of the user, so all in view, all rendering, all animating) and re-runs beginRevealWarmup(). renderedDropCount climbs monotonically; placedHolders grows; frameUpdate's per-holder loops (2320+), applyPerceptualCompensation and updatePowerTier's distance scan all iterate the growing set every frame/tick. Three or four loops is a screen of overlapping fireworks and a GPU particle load the app never budgeted, on a first-run session that is also paying cold camera + VIO + model decode — i.e. the 10-minute thermal bar is under attack in the first two minutes of the app's life, on the one flow every reviewer will exercise. It also compounds FLOW-1's confusion: the promise beat now returns to a floor already covered in fireworks.
ownFindings.fix: Two independent fixes, both needed. (1) Hoist the beat to AppRouter (the FLOW-1 fix) so the loop cannot exist. (2) Make placeRoomDrop idempotent for the demo: have startDemo call manager.clearRoomDrops() before placing, or give placeRoomDrop a `replacingExisting: Bool = false` parameter that the onboarding path passes true. Test: `testOnboardingDemoPlacesExactlyOneFireworksDropAcrossThreeCycles` — drive startDemo→endFireworksDemo three times against a manager seam and assert roomDrops.count == 1 and placedHolders.count == 1 each time; it fails today with 1, 2, 3.

ownFindings.title: ARP-12's buffer-ownership rule was applied to ARKit's buffers but not to ARCore's: SemanticFeed pins the last semanticImage/semanticConfidenceImage across every detach and the whole suspension
ownFindings.trace: GeospatialEngine.update (GeospatialEngine.swift:239-244) stores garFrame.semanticImage and garFrame.semanticConfidenceImage into SemanticFeed via update(labels:confidence:) (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:18-23), which retains both CVPixelBuffers until the next call replaces them. The ONLY site that clears them is setSemanticsActive(false) (GeospatialEngine.swift:181-192), whose first line is `guard on != semanticActive, semanticSupported, let garSession, let configuration else { return }`. disarmSemanticMatte (GeoARSessionManager.swift:395-398) sets semanticFeed.setEnabled(false) — which only makes snapshot() return nil (36) — and does NOT clear the buffers. suspendSession (402-414) cancels tickTask FIRST (408-409) and only then calls disarmSemanticMatte, so the tick that would have driven geospatial.setSemanticsActive(needsSemantics && tier > .idle) (updatePowerTier:1136) never runs again: semanticActive stays true and both buffers stay retained for the entire suspension.
ownFindings.harm: Two ARCore-owned CVPixelBuffers (label + confidence, small, but drawn from GARSession's own recycling) stay pinned for the whole time the camera tab is left and for every governor detach — the exact 'holding a producer's pool buffer past its frame' class ARP-12 was filed for, on the one producer Wave D did not audit. Magnitude is small (two low-resolution planes), which is why it is LOW; it matters because the ARP-12 fix is now advertised as complete and the next author will reasonably assume the buffer-ownership rule is enforced everywhere.
ownFindings.fix: Add `func clear() { lock.lock(); labels = nil; confidence = nil; enabled = false; lock.unlock() }` to SemanticFeed and call it from disarmSemanticMatte instead of setEnabled(false), so shedding the matte releases the producer's buffers on the same edge that stops consuming them. Reorder suspendSession to disarm BEFORE cancelling the tick, or make disarm the single shed point. Test: `testDisarmReleasesSemanticBuffers` — publish two buffers into the feed, hold weak refs, call disarmSemanticMatte, assert both weak refs are nil; fails today (both alive).
